title: Diurnal Temperature Range and Its Association with Mortality and Morbidity in Japan, 2015–2019
abstractText: Abstract While diurnal temperature range (DTR) is a risk factor for mortality, its association with morbidity remains unclear. This study aimed to examine the associations of DTR with mortality and morbidity in Japan and identify vulnerable populations. We collected mortality and emergency ambulance dispatch (EAD) data for all causes, circulatory and respiratory diseases from 47 prefectures in Japan from 2015 to 2019. We employed two-stage time series analyses using Quasi-Poisson regression with distributed lag nonlinear models and multivariate meta-analysis. Increased DTR was a risk factor for mortality and EAD from all causes and respiratory diseases. For circulatory diseases, a positive association was observed only with mortality. The risk for mortality was delayed by 1 day and persisted for 1–3 days, whereas the relative risk for EAD was highest at lag 0. Males showed significantly higher sensitivity to increased DTR for all-cause EAD, while individuals aged 65 years and older were more vulnerable to circulatory and respiratory EAD. For all-cause EAD, the Relative Risk in southern regions was significantly higher than in other regions. Our findings suggest that DTR is an important climate-related risk factor for both mortality and EAD, with variations observed in lag duration, disease, and subgroups.

title: A systematic map of syntheses on anthropogenic noise impacts on wildlife: evidence gaps, policy attention, and quality appraisal
abstractText: As systematic reviews on the effects of anthropogenic noise on wildlife increasingly inform policy, a critical evaluation of this secondary evidence is essential. We assessed the coverage, methodological quality, and policy relevance of existing syntheses in this field. Following a preregistered protocol, we conducted a systematic search using Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, that identified 50 syntheses (systematic reviews, maps, and meta-analyses). Of these 50 syntheses, we included 47 in the bibliometric analysis, 23 in the policy attention analysis, and 44 in the critical appraisal. The included syntheses were published between 2008 and 2025, but mainly in the last six years, and focused on behavioural, physiological, and communication outcomes in animals. Most syntheses looked at the effects of transportation and energy industry activities. Syntheses were most likely to review evidence from marine, followed by terrestrial ecosystems. We found critical gaps in the coverage in terms of their taxonomic scope, with notable underrepresentation of invertebrates, amphibians, and reptiles. Most syntheses were first-authored by researchers based in the United Kingdom, Canada, and the United States. Although many syntheses had authors from more than one country, authors from non-English-speaking countries were largely absent. Almost half of syntheses were cited in policy documents, mainly government policies and regulatory submissions. Syntheses of evidence on marine environments received the most policy citations and urban noise the least. There was no significant difference in quality scores between policy-cited and non-cited syntheses, and most of them are rated low due to methodological and reporting shortcomings. Given these findings, it is critical to fill the synthesis gaps and improve methodology and reporting of future evidence syntheses in this area.

title: Wrist photoplethysmography encodes dietary information
abstractText: Whether wearable photoplethysmography (PPG) contains dietary information remains unknown. We trained a language model on 1.1M meals to predict meal descriptions from PPG, aligning PPG to text. PPG nontrivially predicts meal content; predictability decreases for PPGs farther from meals. This transfers to dietary tasks: PPG increases AUC by 11% for intake and satiety across held-out and independent cohorts, with gains robust to text degradation. Wearable PPG may enable passive dietary monitoring.

Maternal autophagy contributes to grain yield in maize
abstractText: Maize is an important crop species that is cultivated worldwide, and increasing maize yield is one of the major goals of plant breeding. The subcellular degradation and recycling pathway known as autophagy is involved in many plant developmental processes including vegetative growth, reproductive development, seed development, and senescence. Here, we demonstrate that maize autophagy-defective atg10 mutants have delayed flowering and reduced kernel size, weight and number, leading to reduced grain yield. Reciprocal crosses between mutant and parental lines indicate that the maternal plant is the major contributor to the kernel phenotype in atg10 mutants, rather than the seed genotype. We hypothesize that this may be due to detrimental effects on nutrient remobilization from maternal tissue to seeds during kernel development, leading to reduced yield.

title: Distinct Plasmonic and Electronically Mediated Pathways for Vibrational Excitation
abstractText: Abstract Understanding how plasmonic energy is transferred into molecular vibrations at metal–molecule interfaces is essential for controlling plasmon-driven chemistry and surface-enhanced spectroscopies. However, distinguishing vibrational excitation mediated by electronic transitions and vibronic coupling (VC) from plasmon-enhanced Raman vibrational pumping (PERVP) remains challenging because both mechanisms generate nonequilibrium vibrational populations. Here, we combine cryogenic surface-enhanced Raman scattering with controlled surface chemistry to investigate these competing excitation pathways using thionine adsorbed on gold nanostructures. Citrate-stabilized gold nanoparticles exhibit two distinct excitation regimes. The first is characterized by unusually intense anti-Stokes scattering despite weak Stokes emission, with laser-power dependences inconsistent with conventional vibrational pumping. This behavior is attributed to VC facilitated by molecular adsorption geometries that favor metal–molecule electronic coupling and transient charge transfer. The second regime exhibits strong Stokes scattering and superlinear anti-Stokes intensity, consistent with PERVP and molecular optomechanics. In contrast, bromide-containing gold nanorods exhibit a single excitation regime with laser-power dependences closely matching theoretical predictions for PERVP, suggesting preferential molecular dipole alignment with the localized plasmonic field. At cryogenic temperatures, pronounced anti-Stokes blinking and the transient activation of weak or Raman-inactive vibrational modes further reveal dynamic interfacial restructuring associated with bromide adsorption. These findings demonstrate how molecular orientation, interfacial electronic coupling, and surface chemistry influence the dominant vibrational excitation pathway, providing a framework for controlling plasmonic energy transfer at metal–molecule interfaces.

Hospital-based clinical ethics support in Latin America: a scoping review of committee, consultation, and hybrid models
abstractText: Abstract Hospital-based clinical ethics support in Latin America encompasses committees, consultations and integrated service models, but the organizational evidence is dispersed. Objective: To map how these services are structured, accessed and delivered, and what contributions are reported in patient-specific ethical dilemmas. This scoping review followed JBI guidance and PRISMA-ScR. Searches in BVS/VHL, Scopus, PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science and SciELO were supplemented by backward/forward citation tracking, Google Scholar and targeted grey-literature searching. Studies were charted at report level and overlapping hospital publications were linked. The inventory contains 119 reports: 50 empirical, 27 institutional/descriptive and 42 conceptual/theoretical. Of 67 directly linked reports describing operating services, 47 non-overlapping operational analytic units were mapped. These comprised 41 committee-centred units​, three integrated-service, one hybrid, one team-consultation and one individual-consultation unit. End-of-life decisions, treatment proportionality, autonomy and clinical–family disagreements were recurrent themes. Data on access, response times, patient/family participation and evaluated outcomes were inconsistently reported. Regional evidence documents diverse organizational models and reported contributions of clinical ethics support services, although the available studies provide limited evidence on patient-level outcomes and clinical effectiveness.

title: Incidence of Colorectal Cancer After Endoscopic Mucosal Resection: A Multicenter Electronic Health Record Cohort Study
abstractText: Abstract Background Endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR) is the standard treatment for complex colorectal lesions, offering an effective minimally invasive alternative to surgery. However, the incidence of colorectal cancer (CRC) arising after EMR is incompletely characterized across diverse real-world populations. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network. Adult patients (≥ 18 years) who underwent colonoscopy or sigmoidoscopy with EMR between January 2016 and January 2017 were included. Patients with a prior diagnosis of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) or familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) were excluded. The primary outcome was incident CRC, observed annually from 2018 through 2021. Incidence rates were calculated as cases per 1,000 person-years (PYO), stratified by age group, sex, race, and ethnicity. Temporal trends were assessed using annual percentage change (APC) analysis. Results A total of 4,187 patients were included. The overall post-EMR CRC incidence was 11.85 per 1,000 person-years. Incidence was higher in men (13.61) than women (10.28). Marked racial and ethnic disparities were observed: Hispanic/Latino patients had the highest incidence (28.30), compared to non-Hispanic/non-Latino individuals (12.10). By race, Asian patients had the highest incidence (23.38), followed by Black (11.81) and White patients (10.78). Age-stratified analysis identified the highest incidence in the 40–49-year group (42.2 per 1,000 PYO), with lower rates in the 50–59 (7.8) and 60–69 (9.4) groups, increasing again to 16.8 in the 70–79-year group. Temporal analysis revealed a 27.6% decline in incidence from 30.1 in 2018 to 21.8 per 1,000 PYO in 2021. Conclusion Post-EMR CRC incidence varied substantially across racial, ethnic, sex, and age groups, with notable disparities disproportionately affecting Hispanic/Latino and Asian populations, as well as younger adults. These findings underscore the need for risk-stratified, equity-focused surveillance protocols following EMR and call for prospective research integrating procedural, demographic, and molecular data.

title: Pharmacokinetics, tissue residue depletion and withdrawal period estimation for tylosin in geese (Anser anser domesticus) following intravenous, intramuscular, and oral administration
abstractText: Tylosin, a macrolide antibiotic, is used in poultry to treat Mycoplasma-associated respiratory disease and Clostridium perfringens-associated necrotic enteritis. No pharmacokinetic or tissue residue data exist for geese, preventing the establishment of a species-specific withdrawal period.This study characterized plasma pharmacokinetics in sixteen healthy adult male Bilgorajska geese (Anser anser domesticus) using a four-period crossover design following intravenous (5 mg/kg), intramuscular (25 mg/kg), single-dose oral (100 mg/kg), and multiple-dose oral (100 mg/kg q24h × 3 days) administration. Tylosin concentrations were quantified via validated UHPLC–MS/MS and analyzed using non-compartmental methods. Tissue residue depletion in muscle, fat, liver, and kidney was assessed in a separate group of sixteen geese at 10, 24, 48, and 72 hours post-final oral dose, with withdrawal periods estimated using EMA WT 1.4 (MRL = 100 µg/kg).Systemic clearance was 0.81 ± 0.11 L/h/kg, volume of distribution 2.36 ± 0.12 L/kg, and terminal half-life approximately 2 hours across parenteral routes. Absolute bioavailability was 56 ± 19% after IM and 16–17% after oral dosing. No accumulation occurred after three days of oral administration. Liver residues were highest and most persistent; muscle and fat were below MRL by 24 hours, while kidney marginally exceeded MRL at 72 hours. Estimated withdrawal times were 2.91, 4.23, and 7.66 days for muscle, kidney, and liver, respectively, yielding a provisional withdrawal period of 8 days. These exploratory findings provide the first species-specific pharmacokinetic and residue data for tylosin in geese, identifying liver as the marker tissue and demonstrating route-dependent bioavailability differences.

title: To check or not to check: Adolescents’ sourcing practices when writing from multiple texts
abstractText: Abstract Writing from multiple texts is a crucial academic literacy practice at the university level. Therefore, students should learn to attend to, evaluate, and use information about the sources by the time they reach the end of upper secondary school. The present study investigated differences in upper secondary school students’ ( N = 87) sourcing practices when composing a short article based on multiple texts. The data consisted of students’ written articles and log files recording their time spent on the task and revisits to the source texts during the writing task. Based on analyses of sourcing in students’ written articles, five source user profiles were identified: (1) Advanced source users ( n = 18); (2) Elaborative source users ( n = 15); (3) Basic source users ( n = 15); (4) Vague source users ( n = 15); and (5) No-source users ( n = 24). Students in the three more capable profiles incorporated at least once an explicit source-content link into their articles, varying the number of source features used. During the writing task, Advanced source users revisited both more credible texts more frequently than less capable source users. Their composed articles also most often included citations and main claims from both more credible texts. Conversely, the other students who engaged in sourcing revisited and referenced only one more credible text. The results of the present study implicate that students might benefit from differentiated instructional support to accurately and elaborately cite sources in their writing.

title: Needs Assessment: Expanding Perinatal Psychiatry Access Programs to Support Infant Care Professionals and Postpartum Individuals
abstractText: Abstract Background The Perinatal Psychiatry Access Program model (i.e., Access Program) aims to address mental health (MH) inequities among pregnant and postpartum individuals by providing MH training and support to perinatal care professionals. Despite program expansion, perinatal MH and substance use disorders (SUDs) remain significant contributors to postpartum maternal mortality. Collaborating with infant care professionals may enhance detection and access to MH/SUD treatment. This needs assessment explored infant care professionals’ interest in recognizing and responding to the MH/SUD needs of pregnant and postpartum individuals and assessed the degree to which the statewide Massachusetts Child Psychiatry Access Program for Moms (MCPAP for Moms), could meet the needs of these professionals. Methods We conducted four focus groups (n = 33) and 20 interviews (n = 22) with public health professionals, MCPAP for Moms staff, and child-focused professionals. Sessions were transcribed and coded using iterative thematic analysis. Results Although most infant care professionals expressed interest in perinatal MH/SUDs, this interest varied based on their recognition of parental MH as within their purview. Training and systematic support for perinatal MH/SUDs was not common in infant care settings. Conclusions These findings highlight infant care professionals' interest in supporting postpartum individuals with perinatal MH/SUDs as well as the need for an increased prioritization of workforce development to serve the infant care system and ultimately improve the lives of families. Hiring additional staff, including a liaison from the early childhood community, and leveraging existing networks to improve consultation, resource referrals, and communication with infant care professionals is recommended.

title: Computational Compound Prioritization Strategy Incorporating Docking Variability and Interaction Energies Identifies Putative LRH-1 Binders
abstractText: Compound ranking in structure-based virtual screening notoriously yields highly ranked false positive binders due to variable poses or biases in scoring terms. We developed a compound prioritization strategy that utilizes sampled docked poses from contrasting docking approaches (targeted physics-based docking and blind docking with a generative model) against multiple models of the target protein to train a multi-layer perceptron (MLP). The model predicts binders at the orthosteric ligand-binding pocket of the nuclear receptor LRH-1 (NR5A2). Our approach circumvents the reliance on a single docked pose for scoring compounds or individual scoring metrics for compound ranking. In a separate benchmarking set, we observed that the MLP identifies known binders that are chemically dissimilar from the compounds in the training set and is sensitive to single scaffold modifications, making it a potential tool for lead optimization. We applied our strategy to a prospective virtual screening campaign, which resulted in the discovery of four putative LRH-1 binders. We found that a combination of scoring and prediction metrics enriches for the hit compounds across library sizes. In all, this implementation presents a method to leverage structural and experimental data to aid virtual screening for a challenging protein target.

title: Aberrant autophagy–senescence axis drives spontaneous abortion through HSPA6/FOXO1-mediated decidual stromal dysfunction
abstractText: Abstract Abnormal senescence of decidual stromal cells is tightly linked to spontaneous abortion, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly defined. In this study, we found that the senescence level of DSCs in the decidual tissues of patients with recurrent spontaneous abortion (RSA) significantly increased during the first trimester. Using both in vitro and in vivo models, we show that abnormally elevated branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs) reduce autophagic flux, leading to excessive DSC senescence, which mechanistically involves aberrant heat shock protein A6 (HSPA6) upregulation and subsequent the core transcription factor forkhead box O1 (FOXO1) downregulation, thereby predisposing to adverse pregnancy outcomes. Both in vitro and in vivo experiments demonstrated that the reduced macroautophagy/autophagy flux resulting from abnormally elevated branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs) leads to excessive DSC senescence. In vivo studies, intervention with leucine, a key BCAA, promoted uterine senescence and induced adverse pregnancy outcomes in mice. Conversely, restoring autophagy with rapamycin effectively suppressed excessive senescence at the maternal-fetal interface and significantly improved pregnancy outcomes under high-leucine conditions. Therefore, this study demonstrates that excessive senescence at the maternal-fetal interface, resulting from impaired autophagy flux, disrupts pregnancy maintenance via the HSPA6-FOXO1 signaling pathway. These findings highlight the role of metabolic disorders and autophagy imbalance in miscarriage, and offer potential therapeutic strategies for preventing spontaneous abortion.

title: Drift-Driven Microbiome Simplification Generates Reconstructable and Ecologically Cohesive Microbial Communities
abstractText: ABSTRACT Engineering simplified microbial communities that retain function and ecological cohesiveness remains a major challenge because the taxa and interactions required for community establishment are rarely known a priori. Here, we experimentally evaluated drift-driven microbiome simplification as an alternative strategy for generating reduced and reconstructable microbial consortia. Using the tomato rhizosphere as a model system, three source microbial communities were subjected to different dilution bottlenecks and serial propagation. Increasing dilution was the main determinant of community composition and simplification, while repeated passage produced additional reductions in ASV richness, phylogenetic diversity, and evenness. Importantly, diversity loss was not accompanied by a uniform deterioration in bacterial colonization or plant performance, indicating that substantial simplification can occur without a parallel collapse in these system-level properties. Candidate Minimal Microbiome prototypes were selected from endpoint communities, reconstructed as synthetic communities, and their ecological cohesiveness was evaluated through invasion experiments. The reconstructed communities strongly restricted the establishment of the original complex microbial fractions, although invasion success depended markedly on invader identity. The drift-derived communities were at least as resistant to invasion as an independently designed bottom-up synthetic community. Together, these results provide experimental support for drift-driven simplification as a strategy to generate reduced microbial communities whose dominant members can be isolated, reconstructed, and experimentally evaluated. By allowing ecological assembly to generate candidate community configurations before cultivation and reconstruction, this approach provides a complementary route to rational bottom-up design and function-directed top-down microbiome engineering.

Effects of an intensive firefighter training program on a simulated fire-escape staircase climb
abstractText: Abstract To evaluate the effects of a four-week intensive training program on weighted stair-climb performance, 18 participants (17 men, 1 woman) completed 16 training sessions combining strength, power, and endurance work. Pre- and post-intervention assessments included a loaded fire-escape staircase climb test, incremental VO₂max test, 30-s Wingate test, submaximal squat test, anthropometric measures, and the ANTI-Vea attentional task. Linear mixed models were used to assess intervention effects; effect sizes were expressed as Cohen's d . Stair-climb time decreased significantly after training (EMC: −1.26 s; d = − 0.88). Post-intervention performance was predicted by a composite Strength Score ( β std = − 0.65) and Wingate Score ( β std = − 0.35; model R ² = 0.86). High-load squat velocity and power, estimated 1RM, and Wingate mean power improved significantly (all d > 0.67), whereas VO₂max, ventilatory thresholds, and body mass remained unchanged. ANT-I mean reaction time improved ( d z = − 0.59), with a shift from a linear to a quadratic vigilance decrement pattern. In conclusion, four weeks of intensive firefighter training improved stair-climb performance primarily through neuromuscular and anaerobic adaptations. Training programs targeting this task should prioritize explosive strength at task-relevant loads and anaerobic endurance, while dedicated cognitive training may be required to improve higher-order vigilance components.

MambaSleepCVD for prediction of long term cardiovascular outcomes from polysomnography
abstractText: Abstract Long-term cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk prediction remains a major global clinical priority. This study investigates how much prognostic information full-night polysomnography (PSG) carries after explicitly controlling demographic confounding, and whether combining specialized unimodal representations with continuous fusion mechanisms can effectively leverage it. We adopt a modular framework based on Coupled Mamba for simultaneous cross-modal and temporal fusion, capturing long-range dependencies and dynamic interactions between physiological modalities throughout sleep. With this capability we assess whether specialized supervised representations from task-specific unimodal encoders offer prognostic value comparable to task-agnostic multimodal self-supervised pre-training. Validated on the Sleep Heart Health Study (SHHS) dataset, our approach achieves performance comparable to or better than current state-of-the-art architectures in the fully supervised, data-abundant regime, although the cardiac channel alone accounts for most of the discriminative signal. More importantly, we identify a significant age-related bias in the reference dataset that, if left unaddressed, creates a shortcut leading to inflated risk predictions, accounting for a large part of the literature’s reported performance. Ultimately, our findings suggest that supervised unimodal experts integrated through a fusion engine provide a flexible pathway for prognostic risk ranking from sleep recordings, while reliable CVD screening will require independent external cohorts and explicit confounder control.

title: Cellular senescence changes and their association with brain structure in schizophrenia and major depressive disorder
abstractText: Abstract Individuals with schizophrenia (SZ) and major depressive disorder (MDD) may experience accelerated biological aging, potentially linked to cellular senescence and the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). While the SASP index has been reported to be elevated in MDD, its status in SZ and its relationship with brain structure remain unclear. This study investigated whether the SASP index, a composite biomarker-based measure, is elevated in SZ and MDD, and examined its associations with brain-predicted age difference (brain-PAD) and regional brain morphology across SZ, MDD, and healthy controls (HCs). A total of 119 subjects (29 individuals with SZ, 40 individuals with MDD, and 50 HCs) underwent both peripheral blood collection and MRI scanning. First, across all subjects, the effects of diagnostic groups on SASP indices were assessed. Second, associations between age-adjusted SASP indices and brain-PAD were examined within each diagnostic group. Third, exploratory analyses tested associations between SASP indices and subcortical volumes as well as cortical thickness and surface area in each diagnostic group. We found a significant main effect of diagnostic group on SASP indices and significantly elevated SASP indices in both SZ and MDD. Although no significant associations were observed between SASP indices and brain-PAD in any diagnostic group, negative associations were identified in SZ between SASP indices and the surface area of the left transverse temporal gyrus and the right inferior frontal gyrus pars triangularis, regions that play pivotal roles in auditory and language processing alterations observed in SZ. These findings suggest that SASP-related processes may contribute to the neural underpinnings of SZ through localized, rather than global, alterations in brain structure.

title: Peran Guru Pendidikan Agama Islam dalam Menangani Kasus Kenakalan Remaja di SMPQ Pelita Khoirul Ummah Bandar Lampung
abstractText: Kenakalan remaja merupakan salah satu permasalahan yang paling sering dijumpai di lingkungan sekolah menengah pertama, termasuk di SMPQ Pelita Khoirul Ummah Bandar Lampung. Bentuk kenakalan yang muncul antara lain rendahnya kedisiplinan, sikap kurang sopan terhadap teman dan guru, serta rendahnya kesadaran dalam melaksanakan ibadah. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan bentuk peran serta strategi yang digunakan guru Pendidikan Agama Islam (PAI) dalam menangani kasus kenakalan remaja di sekolah tersebut. Penelitian menggunakan metode kualitatif deskriptif dengan subjek penelitian siswa kelas IX tahun ajaran 2025/2026 yang berjumlah 22 siswa. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi, wawancara, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis dengan teknik reduksi data, penyajian data, serta penarikan kesimpulan dan verifikasi, dan keabsahan data diperiksa melalui ketekunan pengamatan dan triangulasi sumber. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa peran guru PAI dalam menangani kenakalan remaja dilaksanakan melalui tiga bentuk tindakan, yaitu preventif (murojaah bersama, ceramah keagamaan, salat dhuha dan zuhur berjamaah), represif (nasihat dan teguran, hukuman ringan yang mendidik, serta pemanggilan orang tua), dan kuratif (pemberian skor pelanggaran hingga pengembalian sementara siswa kepada orang tua). Adapun strategi yang diterapkan bersifat preservatif, yaitu pemberian motivasi dan keteladanan secara konsisten melalui pendekatan personal, sehingga sebagian besar siswa menunjukkan perubahan sikap ke arah yang lebih baik. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa guru PAI di SMPQ Pelita Khoirul Ummah tidak hanya berperan sebagai pengajar, tetapi juga sebagai pembimbing dan teladan yang berkontribusi nyata dalam pembentukan akhlak siswa serta pencegahan kenakalan remaja secara berkelanjutan.

title: Efektivitas Media Audio Visual terhadap Hasil Belajar PAI Siswa Kelas VIII
abstractText: Rendahnya hasil belajar siswa pada mata pelajaran Pendidikan Agama Islam (PAI) mendorong perlunya penggunaan media pembelajaran yang lebih menarik. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui efektivitas media audio visual terhadap hasil belajar siswa kelas VIII SMP Qur’an Pelita Khoirul Ummah Bandar Lampung. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode eksperimen dan desain One Group Pretest-Posttest. Subjek penelitian berjumlah 22 siswa. Data dikumpulkan melalui tes, observasi, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan uji normalitas, paired sample t-test, dan N-Gain. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa ketuntasan belajar meningkat dari 63,64% pada pretest menjadi 100% pada posttest. Uji paired sample t-test memperoleh nilai signifikansi 0,000 < 0,05, sedangkan nilai N-Gain sebesar 0,4871 termasuk kategori sedang. Dengan demikian, penggunaan media audio visual efektif dalam meningkatkan hasil belajar siswa pada mata pelajaran PAI.

title: Tahapan Pengembangan Instrumen Evaluasi Maharah Kalam Berdasarkan Kajian Teoretis dan Hasil Penelitian Terdahulu
abstractText: Evaluating *maharah kalam* (speaking skills) requires instruments capable of measuring speaking proficiency in a valid and reliable manner; however, current practices often rely on assessing comprehension without the use of standardized rubrics. This study aims to outline the stages for developing *maharah kalam* evaluation instruments, drawing upon theoretical frameworks and previous research. Employing a qualitative descriptive approach through a literature review, this study examines theories of language assessment, instrument development models (such as those by Mardapi, the 4D and 3D models, and the ADDIE model), as well as ten studies published between 2021 and 2026. The findings indicate that while existing research typically involves needs analysis, the design of tasks and rubrics, and expert validation, evidence of reliability—particularly inter-rater reliability—is rarely reported. Based on this synthesis, seven development stages are proposed: (1) needs analysis and construct definition; (2) specification and blueprint development; (3) design of tasks and rubrics; (4) expert validation; (5) limited pilot testing; (6) empirical analysis; and (7) revision, final assembly, and reporting. This framework is intended to serve as a guide for educators and researchers in developing systematic and accountable maharah kalam evaluation instruments.

title: Transforming Teacher Competencies in the Era of Generative Artificial Intelligence: Mapping the Research Landscape and Future Research Agenda
abstractText: The rapid development of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) has reshaped educational practices and created new demands for teachers' professional competencies. This study aims to map the global research landscape on teacher competency transformation in the GenAI era through a bibliometric analysis of Scopus-indexed publications. A total of 383 open-access journal articles published between 2023 and 2026 were analysed using performance analysis and science mapping with VOSviewer version 1.6.21. The findings reveal a substantial increase in scientific publications, with approximately 89.3% published in 2025–2026. China emerged as the leading contributor, while Indonesia ranked fifth. The research landscape is primarily structured around artificial intelligence, AI literacy, professional development, teacher training, digital competence, and AI in education. Thematic evolution indicates a shift from foundational discussions of AI literacy and professional development toward empirical investigations of technology acceptance, behavioral intention, decision-making, and academic integrity. The findings highlight the need for comprehensive teacher competency frameworks, effective continuous professional development, and stronger institutional governance to support responsible AI integration. This study contributes to understanding the intellectual development and emerging priorities of research on teacher competencies in AI-enhanced educational environments.

title: Adaptive error management for fault-tolerant quantum computing across hardware-level suppression, system-level diagnosis, and real-time decoding
abstractText: Abstract Fault-tolerant quantum computing reached a milestone in December 2024 when Google’s Willow processor demonstrated below-threshold error correction on a superconducting chip, a result since reproduced on neutral-atom and alternative superconducting platforms. Yet the classical decoders needed to sustain this performance face a scaling challenge: noise becomes increasingly structured and correlated as systems grow, while decoders must respond within microsecond coherence windows. This survey asks whether error suppression, noise diagnosis, and decoding are better treated as one adaptive control problem than as three separate research programs. Drawing on a scoping review of 146 records, it organizes the field into a three-layer taxonomy. Layer 1 (Hardware-Level Suppression) integrates protection into the physical substrate; bosonic cat qubits exponentially suppress bit-flip errors, projecting up to 90% overhead reduction versus surface codes. Layer 2 (Diagnosis) employs probabilistic models and computational intelligence to characterize error sources; neuro-fuzzy architectures and the Bias–Entropy decomposition separate hardware drift from logical faults, subject to an identifiability limit that we characterize. Layer 3 (Real-time Decoding) targets the integration of machine learning within strict latency constraints. Hardware acceleration now approaches superconducting cycle times, which shifts the case for learned decoders from speed toward accuracy under correlated noise; recent advances favor hybrid, physics-informed architectures: Neural Belief Propagation resolves degeneracy issues in quantum low-density parity-check codes by embedding topological constraints directly into the network’s loss function. These results suggest a transition toward closed-loop AI architectures that treat error management as continuous control rather than static algorithm selection.

Numerical modeling of slope stability in hydropower reservoir systems examined through a bibliometric and systematic review
abstractText: Abstract Reservoir-level variations associated with hydropower operation can alter the hydraulic and mechanical response of adjacent slopes, while evidence linking these processes to numerical modeling remains dispersed across operational scenarios and methods. The objective of this study is to integrate the available evidence on reservoir-slope response to water-level variations through bibliometric analysis and systematic technical synthesis, examining operational hydraulic scenarios and the capabilities, applicability, and limitations of numerical and hydro-mechanical modeling approaches. The methodology comprised three phases: (i) literature search and bibliographic corpus construction; (ii) bibliometric analysis and science mapping; and (iii) systematic review and comparative technical synthesis. The search retrieved 479 records; thematic refinement yielded 420 records for bibliometric analysis, and systematic screening retained 163 studies for technical synthesis. Bibliometric analysis showed recent growth and thematic emphasis on rapid-drawdown stability assessment and numerical modeling of reservoir-level fluctuations. The technical synthesis showed that reservoir-level variation does not produce a unique mechanical response; stability depends on the transient balance between external hydrostatic support and internal hydraulic response, conditioned by permeability, drainage, geometry, structural controls, and hydraulic history. Hydraulic lag was identified in 77.9% of studies. Model applicability depended on the failure mechanism, material domain, deformation regime, and engineering output rather than on a universal hierarchy of methods. Formal geotechnical uncertainty analysis of model inputs and spatial variability was reported in only 9.2% of studies. Overall, reservoir elevation or drawdown rate alone cannot define slope condition, and model complexity should be matched to the process and engineering output of interest.

abstractText: Limbah kotoran sapi yang tidak dikelola secara optimal berpotensi menimbulkan permasalahan lingkungan dan menghambat pemanfaatannya sebagai sumber daya yang bernilai ekonomi. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengkaji kondisi sosio-ekologis pengelolaan limbah kotoran sapi serta menganalisis bentuk pemanfaatannya oleh masyarakat peternak di Desa Korleko, Kecamatan Labuhan Haji. Subjek penelitian terdiri atas 81 informan, yaitu 60 peternak, 20 masyarakat terdampak, dan 1 perangkat desa. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan deskriptif kualitatif dengan perspektif sosio-ekologi. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi, wawancara mendalam, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan model interaktif Miles dan Huberman yang meliputi reduksi data, penyajian data, serta penarikan dan verifikasi kesimpulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa pengelolaan limbah masih didominasi praktik konvensional berupa penumpukan limbah padat di sekitar kandang dan pembuangan limbah cair ke saluran drainase tanpa pengolahan. Observasi dan persepsi masyarakat menunjukkan adanya indikasi gangguan terhadap kondisi lingkungan, terutama berupa kekeruhan dan endapan pada saluran air, bau yang menyengat, penyempitan saluran drainase, serta berkurangnya pemanfaatan saluran air oleh masyarakat. Pemanfaatan limbah sebagai pupuk organik juga belum optimal karena sebagian besar limbah digunakan secara langsung atau ditumpuk, sementara program pengomposan yang telah diperkenalkan belum mencapai tahap pengolahan dan penerapan secara berkelanjutan. Temuan ini menunjukkan perlunya penguatan kapasitas peternak, pendampingan teknis berkelanjutan, penyediaan sarana pengolahan, dan kolaborasi antara masyarakat dan pemerintah untuk mendorong pengelolaan serta pemanfaatan limbah yang lebih berkelanjutan dan bernilai ekonomi. Cattle manure waste that is not properly managed has the potential to cause environmental problems and hinder its utilization as an economically valuable resource. This study aims to examine the socio-ecological conditions of cattle manure waste management and analyze its forms of utilization by farming communities in Korleko Village, Labuhan Haji District. The research subjects consisted of 81 informants, including 60 cattle farmers, 20 affected community members, and 1 village government official. The study employed a descriptive qualitative approach from a socio-ecological perspective. Data were collected through observation, in-depth interviews, and documentation, and were analyzed using the Miles and Huberman interactive model, which includes data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. The findings indicate that waste management is still dominated by conventional practices, including the accumulation of solid waste around cattle sheds and the disposal of liquid waste into drainage channels without treatment. Observations and community perceptions indicate potential environmental disturbances, particularly in the form of water turbidity and sediment accumulation in drainage channels, unpleasant odors, narrowed drainage channels, and reduced community use of the water channels. The utilization of manure as organic fertilizer is also not yet optimal, as most waste is either used directly or accumulated, while the composting program that has been introduced has not progressed to the stages of processing and sustainable application. These findings indicate the need to strengthen farmers’ capacity, provide continuous technical assistance, improve waste-processing facilities, and enhance collaboration between the community and government to promote more sustainable and economically valuable waste management and utilization.

title: Population genomic differentiation and demographic history across an elevational gradient in an endemic bromeliad of the Atlantic Forest mountains
abstractText: Abstract Montane elevational gradients provide natural laboratories for investigating how environmental heterogeneity, geographic isolation, and historical climatic dynamics shape demographic history, population divergence, and diversification. Topographic complexity and historical climatic oscillations are major drivers of biodiversity patterns in mountain regions worldwide. The Brazilian Atlantic Forest (BAF), a Neotropical biodiversity hotspot characterized by naturally fragmented montane habitats, provides a suitable system for investigating these processes. Here, we used over a thousand SNPs from populations of Pitcairnia flammea Lindl. (Bromeliaceae) distributed across an elevational gradient to investigate patterns of genetic diversity, population structure, and demographic history. Bayesian and coalescent-based analyses revealed strong population structure, with two major genetic groups broadly contrasting higher-elevation populations with low- and mid-elevation populations, although elevation itself was not directly supported as a driver of genetic divergence. Demographic modeling supported early asymmetric gene flow between the two major genetic groups, with higher migration from Group 2 towards Group 1, followed by subsequent isolation. Divergence-time estimates and heterogeneous changes in effective population size further suggest distinct demographic trajectories during the Middle and Late Pleistocene. Together, our results reveal divergent evolutionary trajectories within a single endemic species and suggest that population differentiation across the Atlantic Forest mountains reflects the combined effects of habitat fragmentation, historical connectivity and isolation, genetic drift, and demographic changes potentially associated with Pleistocene climatic oscillations.

title: Combined Effects of Spinach Leaf Powder and Pomegranate Peel Powder on Hematological Recovery and Iron Status in Phenylhydrazine-Induced Hemolytic Anemia in Rats
abstractText: Iron deficiency anemia (IDA) is a critical public health problem in the world and effective, affordable and sustainable nutritional interventions are needed. This study investigated the hematological efficacy and safety of spinach leaf powder (SLP), pomegranate peel powder (PPP) and their combination in anemic Sprague-Dawley rats induced with phenylhydrazine. Forty-eight male rats (n= 12/ group) with confirmed anemia (baseline Hb < 10.5 g/dL, representing a >30% reduction from pre-induction levels) were divided into four groups: Anemic control, SLP (130 mg/kg/day), PPP (55 mg/kg/day), and SLP+PPP (65 + 28 mg/kg/day) for 48 days. Proximate analysis showed that SLP is very rich in iron (109.2 mg/100 g) and protein (24.5%) while PPP is rich in dietary fiber (32.4%) and bioactive polyphenols. Hematological parameters including hemoglobin, RBC, PCV, serum iron and TIBC showed significant improvements in all treatment groups compared with the anemic control (p = 0.001 for Hb, RBC, and PCV; p < 0.05 for serum iron and TIBC). The SLP+PPP treatment has the best hematological recovery of Hb (15.3 ± 1.0 g/dL), RBC (8.5 ± 0.5 × 10⁶/µL), PCV (45.5 ± 2.3%), and serum Fe (0.88 ± 0.03 μg/dL), despite each component being administered at only half the individual doses. No noticeable toxicity was observed, with no significant changes in WBC (p = 0.450), platelet count (p = 0.620) and relative liver and kidney weights (p > 0.05). These findings provide evidence for synergistic interaction between spinach and pomegranate peel, suggesting that this sustainable plant-based combination is a promising functional food strategy to combat iron deficiency anemia.

abstractText: Background and Aims: Although Shandong Province possesses strong cultural, educational, and infrastructural foundations conducive to the promotion of Rugby Sevens in secondary schools, the development of the sport at the youth level remains limited. This situation is primarily attributed to low awareness and popularity, a shortage of qualified teaching and coaching personnel, inadequate facilities, and the absence of a systematic curriculum and development framework. Furthermore, concerns regarding safety, insufficient policy support, and low student participation continue to hinder the sustainable promotion and development of Rugby Sevens in Shandong secondary schools. The main objective of this research was to develop a guideline to promote youth rugby sevens for secondary schools in Shandong province. Methodology: This research was a mixed-method study; it combines quantitative and qualitative research. To investigate the current situation and development of youth rugby sevens in Shandong Province, the researcher would use a total of 150 school directors and physical education teachers from 30 secondary schools in Jinan City, and the questionnaire validity will be tested for IOC by 5 experts (IOC = 0.75). After that, there will be interviews with 7 experts, and using three rounds of the Modified Delphi method with 21 experts and the connoisseurship method with 7 experts. For questionnaire data analysis would use descriptive data analysis, content analysis for the interview method, and the connoisseurship method. The criteria for Modify Delphi method were median (≥ 3.50) and IQR. (≤ 1.50). Results: The guidelines to promote youth rugby sevens for secondary school in Shandong Province that the researcher has drawn up under the POIC Management principles and Cultural and Social Acceptance element, all 5 elements, total 81 items, divided into 16 items on planning element, 16 items on organizing element, 17 items on implementing element, 17 items on controlling element, and 15 items on cultural and social acceptance element. And 7 experts confirmed that this integrated model not only reflects strong management principles but also responds to the unique social and cultural context of Shandong province. This makes the guidelines both academically innovative and practically applicable for long-term development. Conclusion: They highlighted that the traditional POIC framework ensures strategic alignment, organizational clarity, practical implementation, and accountability, while the newly added Cultural and Social Acceptance dimension provides an innovative breakthrough. This innovation addresses cultural barriers, builds trust among parents and communities, promotes inclusivity, and ultimately ensures the sustainability of Rugby Sevens promotion in secondary schools.

title: Quantifying Hidden Metabolites in 31P NMR Spectra by Physics-Based Spectral Subtraction
abstractText: Abstract NMR spectroscopy enables reliable quantification of the metabolites present in a biological sample. The number of metabolites that can be assessed from NMR spectra is often limited by the intrinsically high complexity of the spectra, arising from the large number of molecules paired with their complex spectral patterns. 31P NMR based metabolomics embraces a reduced yet broad view of the metabolism and significantly facilitates the interpretation of the spectra due to a lower number of signals and a larger chemical shift dispersion. However, full quantification of metabolites can still be hindered by the presence of crowded regions. Here we exploit the fact that NMR lineshapes can be simulated precisely from quantum mechanical calculations for disentangling these crowded regions. Iterative subtraction of accurately simulated and fitted spectra of metabolites presenting isolated signals from the experimental spectrum yields meaningful residuals, enabling assignment and quantification of completely hidden metabolites. This approach ended at a noise-level residual spectrum, granting the full quantification of the 31P NMR spectrum. We implemented this approach in MR-SHIFT, a program developed in this work for spin Hamiltonian simulations and spectral fitting, which was then applied to the fully automated analysis of 31P NMR spectra of mouse tissues.

title: Profilin-regulated actin polymerization dynamics at high monomer concentrations
abstractText: Abstract Actin polymerization in the cytoskeleton drives crucial dynamical biological processes such as cell motility and morphogenesis. Recent experiments 1 show that binding to profilin plays a crucial role in controlling the maximal polymerization speed of F-actin at cellular actin concentrations. These experiments are successfully described by a four reaction kinetic model, which predicts a Michaelis-Menten-like saturation of growth speed at high profilin-actin concentrations. In this work, we further analyze the four reaction model in terms of master equations and using the concept of two polymerization cycles, a pure actin cycle and a profilin-actin cycle and propose further experimental setups to gain access to all kinetic rates of the model. We find that varying the profilin excess leads to a profilin-dependent Michaelis constant for the growth speed. For polymerization against an external force, we identify a unique stall force as an indicator of energetically balanced profilin-driven polymerization, i.e., for the absence of coupling to other chemical processes providing energy input. Calculating length diffusivity (or Fano factor) we show that actin growth becomes much more precise by profilin-regulation and almost reaches precision bounds set by thermodynamic uncertainty relations.

title: Green Transformational Leadership and Green Innovation: The Sequential Mediating Roles of Green Human Capital Management and Work Behavior
abstractText: Organizations seeking environmental improvement need to understand how leaders' environmental priorities are associated with employee capabilities, everyday conduct, and Green Innovation. This study examined the direct and indirect associations among Green Transformational Leadership, Green Human Capital Management, Work Behavior, and Green Innovation, including a sequential mediation pathway. A cross-sectional quantitative survey of 300 purposively selected company employees used a 24-item, five-point Likert questionnaire; the reported data were analyzed with PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4. Green Transformational Leadership was positively associated with Green Human Capital Management (β = 0.406; p < 0.001) and Work Behavior (β = 0.255; p < 0.001), but not directly with Green Innovation (β = 0.041; p = 0.446). Green Human Capital Management was associated with Work Behavior (β = 0.325; p < 0.001) and Green Innovation (β = 0.292; p < 0.001), while Work Behavior was associated with Green Innovation (β = 0.326; p < 0.001). The specific indirect paths through Green Human Capital Management (β = 0.118; p < 0.001), through Work Behavior (β = 0.083; p = 0.001), and sequentially through both mediators (β = 0.043; p < 0.001) were significant. These findings support a statistical explanation in which environmental competency management and work conduct connect leadership orientation with perceived Green Innovation, although the cross-sectional design does not establish causal ordering.

title: Trichrome-based deep learning for quantitative assessment of steatosis, hepatocellular ballooning, and fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis
abstractText: Abstract Aims: This study aimed to develop and evaluate Tri-MASH, a trichrome-based deep learning model for quantitative assessment of steatosis, classic hepatocellular ballooning, and fibrosis, and to explore their spatial relationships. Inflammatory-cell density was evaluated as an exploratory measure. Methods and results: Tri-MASH was trained using 161 training specimens and internally evaluated on 30 randomly selected, nonoverlapping specimens. External evaluation comprised 39 biopsies independently scored by four pathologists and 524 baseline and week-72 biopsies from 262 clinical-trial participants. Internal-validation F1 scores ranged from 78.9% for inflammatory-cell detection to 99.2% for sinusoidal fibrosis. In cohort 1, associations with median pathologist assessments were very strong for steatosis (Rs = 0.85) and fibrosis (Rs = 0.87–0.88) and moderate for ballooning (Rs = 0.55). In cohort 2, exploratory pooled analyses showed moderate associations for steatosis (Rs = 0.52), ballooning (Rs = 0.54), and total and portal-septal fibrosis (Rs = 0.50); confidence intervals and p values were unadjusted for repeated observations within participants. Inflammatory-cell density correlated poorly with lobular inflammation grade (Rs=-0.01 to 0.14). Continuous measurements characterized within-arm longitudinal variation, including variation despite unchanged fibrosis stage. In a selected 50-biopsy subset enriched for NAS ballooning grade 2, case-specific median distances to sinusoidal fibrosis were shorter for ballooned hepatocytes than for lipid droplets ( p < 0.0001). Conclusions: Tri-MASH enables integrated quantitative and spatial analysis of steatosis, classic hepatocellular ballooning, and fibrosis on a single trichrome section. The current data support its use as an adjunctive quantitative research platform rather than a replacement for conventional H&E-based assessment or standalone clinical grading; inflammatory-cell output did not reproduce conventional lobular inflammation grading.

abstractText: Abstract Background Health-related quality of life (HRQoL) has become an important outcome measure following pancreatic resection, particularly because postoperative morbidity remains high despite improvements in perioperative mortality. Although short- and mid-term changes in HRQoL over time have been described, data on long-term outcomes in disease-free survivors remain limited. This study explored longitudinal HRQoL changes in a complete-case subgroup of disease-free survivors after pancreatic resection and contextualized long-term outcomes against general population reference values. Methods This single-centre exploratory longitudinal study assessed HRQoL preoperatively and during follow-up using the validated EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-PAN26 questionnaires. Assessments were grouped into baseline, early postoperative follow-up (1–3 months), and long-term follow-up. Seventeen of 115 initially scheduled patients (14.8%), corresponding to 17 of 67 patients who entered longitudinal HRQoL follow-up (25.4%), were disease-free and had complete data across all three analytical periods. Changes over time were analyzed using Friedman’s test with Kendall’s W as the effect size measure, and the results were descriptively compared with Slovenian general population reference values. All analyses were exploratory and limited to these 17 complete-case disease-free survivors. Results Nominal unadjusted p-values below 0.05 were observed for role functioning ( p = 0.014), social functioning ( p = 0.004), financial difficulties ( p = 0.029), weight loss ( p = 0.002), future worries ( p < 0.001), and planning of activities ( p < 0.001). HRQoL deterioration was most pronounced in the early postoperative period, followed by improvement at long-term follow-up. In the descriptive unmatched comparison, selected functional domains at long-term follow-up approached general population reference values, while insomnia, fatigue, and digestive disturbances persisted. Conclusions In this exploratory analysis of 17 highly selected complete-case disease-free survivors, HRQoL declined in the early postoperative period and improved at long-term follow up in several domains. These findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating and should not be generalized beyond comparable complete-case survivor populations.

Exposure history to volatile anesthetics in patients with malignant hyperthermia: a retrospective analysis of 289 cases
abstractText: Abstract Background: Malignant hyperthermia (MH) is a pharmacogenetic disorder triggered by exposure to volatile anesthetics or depolarizing muscle relaxants. Although anesthetic history is an important clue for identifying MH susceptibility, its clinical significance remains incompletely understood, particularly in Asian populations. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed data from a large institutional MH database. Patients with a Clinical Grading Scale (CGS) score ≥35 were included. Clinical characteristics, anesthetic history, family history, and preoperative findings were collected. Among patients with identifiable anesthetic histories, the number of exposures to volatile anesthetics prior to MH onset was evaluated. Patients were divided into two groups based on whether MH occurred at the first exposure or after previous uneventful exposures. Among patients who developed MH, multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to compare the timing of MH onset-specifically evaluating factors associated with MH occurring at the first exposure versus after previous uneventful exposures to volatile anesthetics. Results: Of 621 registered patients, 436 met the inclusion criteria, and 289 had identifiable anesthetic histories. MH occurred at the first exposure to volatile anesthetics in 232 patients (80%), at the second exposure in 36 patients (12%), and after three or more exposures in 21 patients (7%). The mean number of exposures before MH onset was 1.37 (maximum 11). Approximately 20% of MH patients had undergone previous uneventful anesthesia with volatile anesthetics. In the multivariable analysis comparing the timing of MH onset among patients with MH, the odds of MH occurring during the first exposure to volatile anesthetics were higher in cases occurring in or before 1984 (OR 2.75, 95% CI 1.10–6.86, P = 0.03) and in those occurring during 1985-94 (OR 2.89, 95% CI 1.30–6.41, P = 0.01), compared with cases occurring in or after 1995 (reference category). Age, sex, and succinylcholine use were not significant factors. Conclusions: Although anesthetic history is an important component of preoperative evaluation, approximately 20% of patients with MH in our cohort had experienced one or more previous uneventful exposures to volatile anesthetics before developing MH. These findings indicate that uneventful anesthesia should not be considered sufficient to exclude MH susceptibility, underscoring the need for careful and comprehensive preoperative assessment.

Uji efektivitas menggunakan N-Gain score menunjukkan peningkatan keterampilan berpikir kritis siswa pada kategori sedang (0,61 dan 0,64), sementara uji t berpasangan menunjukkan perbedaan signifikan antara skor pretest dan posttest (p < 0,001). Temuan ini secara statistik mengkonfirmasi bahwa media "Tangga Satuan" efektif dalam menumbuhkan keterampilan berpikir kritis siswa. Studi ini memperluas literatur mengenai pengembangan media pembelajaran matematika dengan menempatkan representasi visual dan interaksi konkret sebagai mekanisme penting dalam meningkatkan pemahaman konseptual dan penalaran siswa. Media ini direkomendasikan untuk digunakan dalam pembelajaran pengukuran panjang guna meningkatkan kualitas pembelajaran dan kemampuan berpikir kritis siswa.

Towards a competence-behaviour-design alignment for educational robotics kits: a theoretical synthesis and development principles
abstractText: Abstract Educational robotics kits (ERKs) are widely used to support competence-oriented technology education, yet their design is rarely grounded in clearly prioritised technological competences and associated learning behaviours. This research, situated in China’s General Technology curriculum, addresses this gap by developing a competence-behaviour-design (C-B-D) alignment for ERKs. The research problem concerns what consistent priority competences and their operationalised learning behaviours are required to guide ERK design. A two-phase mixed-methods approach was adopted. Study 1 used a Delphi-Analytic Hierarchy Process with experienced teachers to prioritise curriculum-defined competences. Materialisation capacity and engineering thinking emerged as highest priorities; within materialisation capacity, ‘knowledge and selection of materials and tools’ and ‘making and processing capability’ were rated equally important, while ‘systems analysis thinking’ was the dominant indicator for engineering thinking. Study 2 undertook document- and artefact-based analysis to identify operationalised learning behaviours corresponding to these competences. Results show that materialisation capacity is predominantly enacted through component selection, modular assembly and basic structural testing, whereas engineering thinking is mainly elicited through functional evaluation, system-level assembly and the design of complete functional structures. The findings characterise priority technological competence as a coherent core of systematic understanding and making, and the associated behaviours as a concrete repertoire of design-and-build actions that bridge precise hands-on making with system-level problem solving. The study contributes a theoretical model of C-B-D alignment and a set of theory-informed ERK design guidelines with feature-behaviour mappings, offering practical guidance for competence-aligned curriculum implementation and product development in technology education contexts internationally, and supporting future empirical evaluation.

abstractText: Abstract Objective To identify the prevalence and severity of overuse shoulder symptoms in elite youth handball players. Methods Six-hundred and sixty (52.3% boys) elite youth handball players were followed prospectively for one season during the seasons 2016-17, 2017-18, 2018-19, and 2019-20. Players completed standardized questionnaires throughout the season and reported any overuse shoulder symptoms. The Western Ontario Shoulder Instability Index (WOSI) questionnaire was distributed five times per season. Latent class analysis (LCA) was carried out to identify different symptom patterns. Results Of 660 athletes, 148 (22.4%) (50% boys, age: 14.1 ± 0.7 years) reported shoulder problems in at least one WOSI questionnaire. The average symptom severity was 457.8 ± 352.0 points (range 4 to 1834). The questions with the highest average scores were about the lack of strength (31.3 ± 27.5), the concern that the shoulder will get worse (29.5 ± 28.5), and clicking, cracking, or snapping of the shoulder (29.3 ± 30.9). No statistically significant sex-related differences were identified across the four WOSI domains. LCA showed no discernible pattern of symptom distribution. Conclusion The prevalence of overuse shoulder symptoms is high and presents as a multi-faceted problem in elite youth handball. The WOSI questionnaire indicates symptom severity rather than distinct symptom patterns.

title: Electric Field Catalysis and the Metabolic Origin of Life
abstractText: Abstract Metabolic theories for the origin of life postulate that chemical reaction networks emerged spontaneously from geochemistry and grew more complex due to positive feedback effects in catalysis. However, experimentally establishing protometabolic networks has proven challenging. In this Perspective, we make the case for electric field catalysis at charged aqueous interfaces as a crucial overlooked element for initiating protometabolic networks, an initial constraint that foreshadows the eventual takeover of electrostatic catalysis by enzymes. We first overview types of positive feedback relevant to the early evolution of metabolism, the theory of electric field catalysis, and its dominant role in enzyme catalysis. We then examine recent experiments and calculations highlighting the ability of external electric fields to enable nonenzymatic analogues of challenging metabolic reactions in micro- to millisecond reaction times. An underexplored mode of small molecule catalysis (reorientation catalysis) that can only operate in external electric fields is proposed to make positive feedback within prebiotic reaction networks more achievable. By embodying electrostatic catalysis, compartmentalization, and ion concentration gradients, charged aqueous interfaces prepattern three fundamental features of biology, making them a preferred environment for a metabolic origin of life. Making robust progress on the origin of life may surprisingly require exploring the nascent area of electric field-mediated chemistry at aqueous interfaces. Life does not use electric fields to catalyze its metabolic network by accident.

title: Craniofacial Anthropometry and Facial Indices among Nigerian Individuals with Down Syndrome: A Comparative Cross-Sectional Study
abstractText: Down syndrome is associated with characteristic craniofacial morphology, yet population-specific anthropometric data from Nigeria remain limited. This study compared craniofacial dimensions and facial indices between Nigerian individuals with Down syndrome and apparently healthy controls. A comparative cross-sectional study conducted in Jos, Nigeria, included 30 individuals with Down syndrome and 60 controls aged 4–24 years. Bizygomatic breadth, morphological facial height, and morphological upper facial height were measured using direct anthropometry. Morphological facial and upper facial indices were calculated from these measurements. Group differences were assessed using independent-samples t-tests, with mean differences, 95% confidence intervals, and Cohen’s d reported. Bizygomatic breadth was lower among participants with Down syndrome than among controls (118.4 ± 9.73 versus 121.5 ± 8.59 mm), although the difference was not statistically significant (p = .126; d = 0.35). Morphological facial height (98.67 ± 9.58 versus 103.8 ± 9.02 mm; p = .015; d = 0.55) and morphological upper facial height (54.87 ± 6.27 versus 59.40 ± 5.12 mm; p < .001; d = 0.82) were significantly lower in the Down syndrome group. Morphological facial and upper facial indices were also significantly lower (p = .009 and p < .001, respectively), with the largest effect observed for the morphological upper facial index (d = 1.04). Overall, differences were more pronounced in vertical facial dimensions and facial proportions than in transverse facial width. These findings expand population-specific anthropometric evidence and support the usefulness of direct craniofacial anthropometry for characterizing the facial phenotype of Down syndrome among Nigerian individuals.

title: Assessment Reform for Introduction to Sociology from the Perspective of the Field Classroom: A Fuzzy Comprehensive Evaluation Framework
abstractText: Assessment reform is central to turning the field classroom from an occasional activity into a durable mechanism of sociological learning. Drawing on the reform of Introduction to Sociology, this article explains how process-based field assignments and summative examination tasks can be aligned around knowledge, competence, and value formation. It then introduces a fuzzy comprehensive evaluation framework whose indicators and weights come directly from the assessment scheme. The framework converts cohort-level score distributions into membership vectors and returns diagnostic evidence to teaching. The reform shows that field-based questioning and assignments help students connect theory with everyday life, strengthen research awareness, and make value-oriented education concrete. Experiential learning, constructive alignment, and transparent evaluation should therefore be designed as one system.

The Use of Memes as a Medium of Expression for Boy Group Treasure Fans on Social Media X
abstractText: This study examines how fans of the South Korean boy group TREASURE use memes as a medium of expression on social media X, particularly in the context of the TREASURE TOUR [PULSE ON] IN JAKARTA. Employing a descriptive qualitative approach, the study applies Roland Barthes’ semiotic framework to interpret the denotative and connotative meanings embedded in memes. Data were collected through digital observation and documentation of relevant posts on X using concert-related keywords and hashtags. Purposive sampling was used to select memes containing visual and verbal signs associated with fans’ expressions and concert experiences. The analysis categorizes the memes into three phases: before, during, and after the concert. The findings reveal that memes serve as symbolic communication through which fans express enthusiasm, anxiety, panic, happiness, nostalgia, longing, and solidarity. Before the concert, memes predominantly represent anticipation and anxiety surrounding ticket purchases; during the concert, they communicate happiness, euphoria, and emotional closeness to the idols; and after the concert, they convey nostalgia, longing, and emotional exhaustion. Through their denotative and connotative meanings, these memes transform individual concert experiences into shared expressions of fandom identity and collective belonging. This study contributes to digital communication and fandom studies by demonstrating how memes function not merely as entertainment content but also as culturally situated forms of emotional expression and symbolic interaction within the TREASURE fandom

title: Analysis of blood components and the mechanism of anti-pharyngitis and gut microbiota regulation in Ardisia crenata and its relatives
abstractText: This study comprehensively integrated network pharmacology, molecular docking, and gut microbiota analysis to explore the anti-pharyngitis targets and pathways of Ardisia crenata Sims (ZSG), Ardisia crenata Sims var.bicolor (Walk) (HLS) and Ardisiacrispa (Thunb.) (BLJ), and to investigate their underlying mechanisms. PPI networks and “herb-component-target-disease” networks were constructed, followed by GO and KEGG enrichment analysis. Molecular docking demonstrated strong binding affinity between the active components and the core targets. Additionally, changes in gut microbiota and endogenous metabolites in rats were analyzed by combining 16S rDNA high-throughput sequencing and untargeted metabolomics. The results revealed that the central targets are SRC, TNF, PIK3CA, STAT3, JAK2. KEGG analysis highlighted notable involvement of the PI3K/AKT, Rap1, Ras, Estrogen signaling pathways. Moreover, all three herbs were found to modulate the gut microbiota to some extent, contributing to the alleviation of microbial dysbiosis. In conclusion, ZSG, HLS and BLJ exert anti-pharyngitis effects through multi-target and multi-pathway mechanisms.

title: Knowing the better, believing the worse: a commitment account of epistemic supererogation
abstractText: Abstract Epistemic supererogation involves going beyond what epistemic rationality requires. If some beliefs can be epistemically supererogatory, then others are epistemically suboptimal yet still rational. In ethics, knowingly doing the suboptimal is commonplace—we often spend money on ourselves rather than giving it to charity. By contrast, existing accounts of epistemic supererogation deny that one could knowingly adopt an epistemically suboptimal attitude. I challenge this assumption and develop a commitment-based account of epistemic supererogation. I focus on cases involving religious, moral, practical, or interpersonal commitments, where the evidence allows more than one rational attitude. In these cases, a longstanding commitment can help explain why someone reasonably sticks with a belief that is epistemically suboptimal. I then consider two ways of explaining this: one on which the belief remains rational because it fits the evidence well enough, and another on which practical factors affect epistemic rationality. This account strengthens the analogy between ethics and epistemology by showing that, in some cases, we can knowingly—and rationally—decline to take the epistemically best option.

title: A hybrid vision transformer–CNN ensemble with radiomics fusion for robust cross-dataset breast cancer detection in mammography
abstractText: Abstract Breast cancer is among the leading causes of cancer-related mortality in women worldwide. Early detection through mammograms can significantly increase the chances of survival. However, mammogram classification remains a challenging task due to subtle lesion features and variations across patients and datasets. Therefore, classic convolutional neural networks (CNNs) fail to generalize across different mammographic sources. In this paper, the proposed method is a hybrid Vision transformer and CNN ensemble learning framework integrated with feature fusion for robust cross-dataset classification. The framework consists of a dual-branch feature extractor that fuses a deep CNN for local texture extraction with a Vision transformer (ViT) for global context extraction, while simultaneously extracting handcrafted radiomics features (shape, intensity, and texture) from the lesion region. Then, deep and radiomics features are fused and fed to a stacked ensemble learning classifier comprising XGBoost, SVM, and LightGBM, with a logistic regression meta-learner for performance optimization and overfitting reduction.The proposed framework is also robust across datasets, achieving AUC scores of 0.938 and 0.925 when trained on CBIS-DDSM and evaluated on INbreast, and when trained on INbreast and evaluated on CBIS-DDSM, respectively, demonstrating strong generalization under domain-shift conditions. The proposed fusion model demonstrates promising potential for robust and reliable use in clinics. On the combined CBIS-DDSM and INbreast dataset, the proposed framework achieved an average accuracy of 96.3%, average MCC of 0.928, and average AUC of 0.983 across the five validation folds. The best-performing fold achieved a peak accuracy of 96.9%, peak MCC of 0.936, and peak AUC of 0.986.

Unraveling the Anti-HCV Mechanism of the Ethyl Acetate Fraction of Vitex cofassus via Integrated Network Pharmacology and Molecular Dynamics Simulation
abstractText: To address the growing health burden posed by the hepatitis C virus (HCV), the present study employed computational approach to predict the medicinal properties of Vitex cofassus. Liquid chromatography-high resolution mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS) analysis of its ethyl acetate leaf fraction identified 37 drug-like compounds. Network pharmacology predicted 201 biological targets, with key proteins such as STAT3, IL6, SRC, AKT1, EGFR, HSP90AA1, and TNF-α being central to the proposed mechanism of action. Functional enrichment analyses pointed to involvement in chemical response, intracellular signaling, stress, and regulated cell death, with molecular functions linked to kinase activity and ATP binding. KEGG analysis further associates targets with key pathways in cancer, viral infection, and metabolic disease. Picrocrocin and flavonoids such as isorhamnetin and apigenin were predicted as potential inhibitors of HCV-related proteins (STAT3 and SRC, respectively). While these in silico findings provide a rational basis for further investigation, the present findings remain predictive and require experimental validation to confirm actual anti-HCV efficacy.

title: Bacillus subtilis as a heterologous host for production and secretion of a hyperthermostable archaeal subtilisin-like protease
abstractText: Abstract Pernisine is a subtilisin-like protease from the hyperthermophilic archaeon Aeropyrum pernix . Its ability to degrade resistant protein substrates such as prion proteins makes this protease attractive for industrial applications. Here, we used Bacillus subtilis as a heterologous host for expression and secretion prepropernisine, a precursor of pernisine. The native secretion signal peptide of prepropernisine was replaced with a signal peptide of native B. subtilis preprosubtilisin E to achieve efficient secretion. Among the four promoters tested, xylose-inducible promoter yielded the highest level of propernisine production, with a titer of 175 mg per l of culture. The produced propernisine was purified from the culture medium using a combination of ultrafiltration, anion-exchange chromatography, and heat treatment. Approximately 115 mg of propernisine with 80% purity was obtained per liter of culture, representing a 10-fold higher yield than previously achieved with other heterologous hosts. Activated pernisine obtained from B. subtilis exhibited remarkably high thermostability, with optimal activity at temperatures above 90 °C and across a pH range of 7 to 9. In addition, it retained approximately 60% of initial activity after autoclaving and efficiently degraded collagen and meat. The stability and performance of pernisine from B. subtilis were nearly identical to that of pernisine produced in Escherichia coli . Overall, these findings demonstrate that B. subtilis is a promising host for further optimization of cultivation conditions and scale-up to controlled bioreactor cultivation, to achieve production of pernisine at industrial level. Key points • Bacillus subtilis efficiently produced and secreted recombinant propernisine. • Propernisine was readily purified from the culture medium. • Activated pernisine exhibited high thermostability and efficient meat hydrolysis.
