Analysis of interfacial force interaction in the internal polymer flow in the hot end of material extrusion additive manufacturing
abstractText: Abstract To better understand the polymer flow physics through the hot end of a material extrusion additive manufacturing process, a volume of fluid multiphase computational fluid dynamics model (CFD) was formulated to integrate the effect of interfacial forces in the air gap between the heating wall and the melting filament. The model was validated by developing a measurement system that captures the extrusion dynamics, which was quantified in terms of feeding force by using two load cells rated at 5 kg and 20 kg as force sensors and a 1 kg load cell to measure extrudate mass. The CFD experimental validation setup presents a detailed method for integrating an inline force measurement system into a commercial 3D printer, requiring minimal modifications to the printhead and gantry head arrangement. The CFD model result, validated against experimental data, follows more closely the measured feeding force of the 5 kg load cell than the 20 kg load cell. The experimental results further show that lower-rated load cells (5 kg) are more precise at low feeding rates, while higher-rated load cells (20 kg) are better for higher extrusion forces. The CFD analysis of the internal flow through the hot end revealed fascinating actionable insights for exploiting interfacial tension effects for the design of the hot end and extrusion system, enabling faster and more reliable printing. The new understanding of the interaction between thermofluid and interfacial tension can inform process parameter control and the design of desktop 3D printers.

title: Analysis of Fourth-Grade Students’ Ability to Understand Fraction Word Problems at SD Negeri 168 Pekanbaru
abstractText: Background: Understanding fraction word problems requires students to interpret written information and relate it to mathematical representations and number magnitude. Aim: This study described the initial performance of Grade IVB students at SD Negeri 168 Pekanbaru on three indicators: interpreting story information as fractions, comparing unit fractions, and ordering unit fractions. Methods: A quantitative descriptive analysis was conducted using the recorded pre-cycle assessment scores of 23 students on 6 October 2026. The assessment comprised five multiple-choice and five open-ended items; descriptive statistics summarized the overall scores and percentage attainment for each indicator. Results: The mean score was 43.22, with a minimum of 6 and a maximum of 83. Nineteen students (82.61%) scored below the assessment threshold of 75. Attainment was 55.98% for interpretation, 35.43% for comparison, and 33.26% for ordering. Conclusion: The relatively lower attainment on comparison and ordering tasks identifies priorities for subsequent instruction. These descriptive data do not establish the causes of students’ difficulties or the effectiveness of the planned Directed Reading Thinking Activity strategy.

abstractText: Purpose: Coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS) form a group ofGram-positive cocci united by their lack of the virulence factor coagulase. Methicillin-resistant CoNS refers to strains of CoNS that has developed resistance to methicillin. The aim of this study was to determine the prevalence of MR-CoNS within Irrua Specialist Teaching Hospital (ISTH), antibiogram and molecular studies of the isolates to acertain the how CoNS which were believed to be non pathogenic acquired some pathogenic traits. Materials and Methods: A total of 299 swabs were collected from different departments in ISTH and processsed using standard microbiological procedures. The 16S rRNA sequencing was conducted on six MR-CoNS isolates. Findings: Results revealed a prevalence of 12% for MR CoNS. The distribution of the MR-CoNS isolates within ISTH revealed thus; fomites (38%), cleaners (24%), patients (16%), nurses (13%), and doctors (8%) while 5% of MR-CoNS possessed nuc, 49% possessed mecA, 41% had blaZ, while 21% had pvl genes respectively. Results of the antibiogram revealed 96% of the isolates were resistant to cloxacillin, while vancomycin and linezolid were the best drug of choice because all isolates were sensitive to these two antibiotics. title: Application of Calcium Salts and Organic Acid Dip Treatments to Improve Quality of Fresh-Cut Potatoes
abstractText: Fresh-cut potatoes are a highly perishable food product due to enzymatic browning, moisture loss, tissue softening and rapid metabolic activity caused by wounding during cutting. The present research was designed to assess the effect of four different dipping treatments: 2% calcium lactate combined with 2% ascorbic acid (T₁), 2% calcium lactate combined with 2% citric acid (T₂), 2% calcium chloride combined with 2% ascorbic acid (T₃), and 2% calcium chloride combined with 2% citric acid (T₄), along with an untreated control (T0), on the physicochemical quality of fresh-cut potatoes during refrigerated storage of 21 days. Slices were dipped in the dipping solutions for 3 minutes followed by packaging in sealed polyethylene bags and storage at 5 ± 1 °C. Samples were analyzed for titratable acidity (TA), pH, total soluble solids (TSS), firmness, weight loss % and color after every 7 days of storage. T₁ gave the best overall balance of firmness, acidity retention and surface color, being the only treatment that significantly increased firmness over the control, whereas T₄ was more effective in limiting changes in pH and TSS. However, weight loss was higher in all treated samples than in control. These findings suggest that application of calcium lactate combined with ascorbic acid can prove to be a promising approach for maintaining the quality of fresh-cut potatoes in refrigerated storage

Autopsy findings after SARS-CoV-2 vaccination: a German national registry study
abstractText: Abstract Autopsies are the foundation of evidence-based medicine and gold standard for determining causes of death. A potential causal relationship between COVID-19 vaccination and death remains a subject of debate, however multidisciplinary, multicentric national autopsy studies are missing. N = 486 eligible SARS-CoV-2 vaccinated autopsy cases from 14 German pathology, neuropathology and legal medicine university centres between 2021 and 2024 were available via the German National Autopsy Registry. For comparison COVID-19 autopsies were included ( n = 385 cases, all performed before the vaccination campaign in Germany started). A previously established causality algorithm was applied in a consensus assessment of potential causality between vaccine administration and an adverse event following immunization (AEFI). N = 176 cases with a post vaccination interval ≤ 28d were included into analyses. In a single case of allergic reaction, in 5/8 cases of either myocarditis ( n = 4 cases) or perimyocarditis ( n = 1 case), and 9/26 cases of thromboembolism, the consensus process resulted in a potential AEFI in these cases, but no definite causality. In n = 3 cases in which the cause of death remained unclear after autopsy, no potential AEFI could be established. In SARS-CoV-2 positive autopsy cases without vaccination, thromboembolism was documented as cause of death in 18/385 cases and myocarditis in 2/385 cases. In conclusion, autopsies are a valuable tool to assess adverse effects. Currently, post vaccination autopsy numbers are too low to draw conclusions on the general population or to identify rare AEFI signals. As part of pandemic preparedness, international guidelines for post vaccination autopsy procedures, diagnostics and interpretation are necessary. Autopsy registries can support this collective effort.

title: Pulmonary vascular abnormalities in Long COVID: a radiological perspective
abstractText: Abstract Background Post-COVID-19 condition (Long COVID) has emerged as a major public health challenge, with survivors frequently reporting persistent dyspnea, fatigue, and exercise intolerance. While initial radiological research focused on parenchymal lung disease, a paradigm shift has identified pulmonary vascular abnormalities—specifically endotheliitis, microthrombosis, and maladaptive angiogenesis—as critical drivers of the Long COVID phenotype. Main Body The disease is characterized by “endotheliitis,” where direct viral entry via ACE2 receptors precipitates a pro-coagulant state and the formation of in situ microthrombi. This is further complicated by immunothrombosis involving neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) and the presence of amyloid-like fibrin microclots that are resistant to natural breakdown. Additionally, structural remodeling through intussusceptive angiogenesis and “vascular pruning” (the loss of distal capillaries) reduces the effective surface area for gas exchange. Conventional CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA) often fails to detect these microvascular changes, despite patients exhibiting severe symptoms. However, advanced modalities provide deeper insights. Dual-energy CT (DECT) reveals persistent, wedge-shaped perfusion defects even in morphologically normal lung parenchyma. Quantitative CT (QCT) allows for the measurement of “vascular pruning,” showing a significant reduction in small vessel volume (PBV5). Hyperpolarized xenon-129 MRI (Hp-XeMRI) has identified a hallmark Red blood cell (RBC):barrier defect, indicating impaired gas transfer from the alveoli to red blood cells—a finding that persists even when standard CT and pulmonary function tests are normal. Functional techniques like V/Q SPECT and phase-resolved functional lung (PREFUL) MRI further confirm a “mottled” perfusion pattern indicative of diffuse small vessel vasculopathy. Short conclusion This review emphasizes that Long COVID involves a distinct vascular phenotype that requires functional and quantitative imaging for accurate diagnosis. Adherence to the 2025 international consensus guidelines—recommending imaging 3 months post-infection and the use of paired inspiratory/expiratory protocols—is essential for standardizing care and differentiating vascular from airway-related symptoms.

abstractText: Abstract Syngas production via dry reforming of methane (DRM) represents a promising route for the valorization of carbon-based molecules, CH4 and CO2, in the emerging decarbonization era. However, the harsh operating conditions required by DRM demand highly active and robust catalysts to exploit this process for hydrogen production. In this context, the rational design of thermally stable catalysts with enhanced resistance to deactivation becomes essential. Herein, we focus on elucidating the structural and morphological evolution of Ni-, Ni–Co-, and Ni–Fe-doped titanates with a perovskite framework during guest cation incorporation and subsequent exsolution. Structural, compositional, and surface modifications were investigated by XRD, SEM, EDX, XAFS, N2 physisorption, and XPS. The catalytic performance of the exsolved materials was evaluated in DRM. The Ni-doped titanate (LSTNO-H) exhibited higher catalytic activity than Ni/γ-Al2O3 for CO2 conversion, reaching 80% conversion at 708 °C compared to 715 °C under short-term tests. However, the titanates still show room for improvement in long-term activity and durability. To elucidate the mechanisms governing catalyst deactivation, DRM tests were performed under diluted conditions, enabling a comparative assessment of structural and surface changes during reaction. Under such conditions, catalyst deactivation was mainly associated with nanoparticle sintering, with partial metal oxidation potentially contributing to activity loss, while no significant carbon deposition was detected. In contrast, the benchmark Ni/γ-Al2O3 catalyst showed carbon deposition, although no measurable deactivation occurred under the investigated conditions. Overall, this study highlights the potential of exsolution-based titanates for DRM while providing insights into the deactivation behavior of exsolved Ni under the investigated conditions.

Occurrence and Environmental Weathering of Agricultural Microplastics on Beaches across Japan: Insights into Surface Mineralization and Metal Binding
abstractText: Abstract We investigated the coastal occurrence and environmental weathering of microplastics derived from polymer-coated fertilizers (PCFs) across Japan. A field survey along the Japanese coastline revealed that PCF-derived microplastics are widely distributed on beaches throughout the country, indicating that agricultural microplastics have dispersed far beyond agricultural landscapes. Compositional analysis showed that these particles consist predominantly of polyolefins (∼70%) and polyurethanes (∼30%) and commonly exhibit oxidative degradation accompanied by iron enrichment. Bulk elemental analysis demonstrated positive correlations between iron and multiple heavy metals. Micro-X-ray fluorescence mapping using a focused 20-μm beam showed that chromium is heterogeneously distributed on the plastic surface and spatially associated with iron, while X-ray absorption spectroscopy indicated its occurrence in ferrihydrite-like phases or as chromite. Although detailed spectroscopic evidence was obtained from a single selected particle, the widespread occurrence of PCF-derived microplastics and their observed metal enrichment suggest that similar geochemical processes may occur at other coastal sites. By linking nationwide field observations with process-level characterization, this study shows that microplastics have the potential to transition from inert debris to geochemically reactive substrates after coastal deposition.

title: SCAN: a cross-species single-cell transcriptome resource for domestic animals—revealing divergent spermatogenesis in avian and mammalian systems
abstractText: Abstract Background Despite the astonishing growth of livestock single-cell transcriptome data, its full potential is severely limited by the lack of specialized functional databases and annotation tools. The ability to systematically integrate, standardize, and deeply interpret livestock single-cell data remains very limited. Results This study constructed SCAN, a high-quality resource platform integrating over 2.1 million single-cell datasets from six livestock species ( Sus scrofa , Gallus gallus , Bos taurus , Bos grunniens , Ovis aries , and Oryctolagus cuniculus ) and a representative model organism ( Danio rerio ). This dataset covers 33 tissue types and 155 cell types, providing differential gene expression profiles for each cell type. Based on this platform, we developed standardized analysis pipelines and visualization tools, and established a livestock marker gene library and a high-quality chicken single-cell annotation reference dataset (CARD). In addition, to demonstrate the utility of the platform, we used SCAN to perform a cross-species single-cell comparison of spermatogenesis between avian and mammalian species. The analysis showed that the early stages of spermatogenesis were relatively conserved across species, whereas differences increased at the later stages; chicken SPT and sperm were significantly enriched in catabolism-related pathways. These observations suggest that the late stages of chicken spermatogenesis may employ a metabolic strategy distinct from that of mammals, but the underlying mechanisms remain to be validated by functional experiments. Conclusions This study provides a unified and standardized resource platform (SCAN) for livestock single-cell data, greatly facilitating data access, cell annotation, and downstream biological exploration, thereby enabling downstream biological discovery—as exemplified by the spermatogenesis study presented in this research. The SCAN database is freely and permanently available at http://www.scanimalsdb.bio-zz.cn .

title: Comparative Evaluation of Machine Learning Models for Credit Card Approval Prediction Using Class Imbalance Handling Methods in the PyCaret AutoML Framework
abstractText: Credit card approval processes are often performed manually, leading to inefficiencies, higher operational costs, and inconsistent decision-making. This study comparatively evaluates several machine learning models under different class imbalance handling strategies to predict credit card approval using the PyCaret AutoML framework. Two experimental scenarios were conducted on a dataset of 25,128 credit card applications, namely PyCaret's built-in SMOTE-based imbalance handling and random undersampling. In the SMOTE-based scenario, the Random Forest model achieved high accuracy, but its recall for the minority class was only 36.11%. In contrast, random undersampling produced more balanced performance, with the Gradient Boosting model achieving 100% recall. These findings indicate that class imbalance handling plays a critical role in credit card approval prediction, and that random undersampling provides more reliable minority-class detection than PyCaret's built-in SMOTE approach for the evaluated dataset.

abstractText: ABSTRACT Numeracy is an essential competency that requires students to understand quantitative information, apply mathematical concepts, and make decisions based on real-life situations. This study aimed to describe the difficulties experienced by students at Islamic junior secondary schools (Madrasah Tsanawiyah, MTs) in Jambi City when solving numeracy problems. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed, involving 25 eighth-grade students selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using five contextual numeracy problems covering percentages, statistics, proportional reasoning, plane geometry, and numerical decision-making, together with classroom observations and semi-structured interviews involving six students and two mathematics teachers. The data were analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing, with findings corroborated through triangulation. The results showed that the students’ mean score was 54.4, with 52% falling into the low and very low categories. The predominant difficulties involved understanding problem contexts (72%), mathematical modeling (64%), interpreting results in context (60%), and calculation procedures (48%). Numerical decision-making problems had the lowest completion rate (18%), whereas percentage problems had the highest completion rate (68%). Interview findings indicated that limited practice with non-routine contextual problems and constraints on instructional time were associated with these difficulties. Therefore, mathematics instruction should incorporate contextual numeracy problems more regularly and encourage students to explain their solution steps and interpret results in context. abstractText: Abstract Colorectal liver metastases (CLM) exhibit distinct histopathological growth patterns (HGPs) at the metastasis-liver interface, clinically relevant for prognosis and potential predictive value. This study investigates the feasibility of using Fluorine-18 Fluorodeoxyglucose Positron Emission Tomography Computed Tomography ( 18 F-FDG PET/CT) to preoperatively classify HGPs in CLM and secondly investigate PET parameters as prognostic markers for overall survival (OS). In a prospective study at Umeå University Hospital (June 2013-December 2017), 78 patients with resectable CLM underwent contrast-enhanced liver MRI and 18 F-FDG PET/CT imaging. HGP classification was performed on tissue sections according to 2017 international guidelines. PET features (SUV mean [standardised uptake value], SUV max , metabolic tumour volume [MTV] and first-order texture metrics) were analysed to distinguish encapsulating (eHGP) from replacement (rHGP) patterns. In pretreated patients, multivariate logistic regression including both metabolic and texture parameters identified significant associations for parameters from the fixed level threshold algorithm (VuePoint Sharp IR) with small odds ratios. Overall, PET parameters showed limited ability to discriminate between eHGP and rHGP. OS was superior with eHGP versus rHGP (log-rank p = 0.045). In chemonaïve patients, SUV-based metrics showed unadjusted exploratory associations with OS after liver surgery, varying by reconstruction/delineation and were not significant after correction for multiple testing. FDG-PET-derived parameters were not reliably associated with HGP and did not support non-invasive HGP prediction in this cohort. eHGP was associated with superior survival, underscoring the value of HGP assessment for prognostication while alternative non-invasive biomarkers remain to be identified.

abstractText: This study was motivated by the persistence of bullying in the school environment, which is often perceived as a joke, particularly in the form of teasing related to students’ family backgrounds. Such behavior can have psychological effects and disrupt victims’ social relationships. This study aims to analyze the psychological impacts experienced by bullying victims, describe the forms of bullying that occur, and examine the implementation of Guidance and Counseling services in addressing and preventing bullying among students at SMA Negeri 1 Sutera, Pesisir Selatan Regency. This study employed a qualitative approach with a descriptive method. The research informants consisted of two students as key informants who were victims of bullying and three additional informants, namely a Guidance and Counseling teacher, a physical education teacher, and a homeroom teacher. Data were collected through observation and interviews and analyzed through data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing. The results showed that bullying affected the psychological conditions of the victims, as indicated by decreased self-confidence, feelings of sadness, anger, fear, and discomfort, reduced trust in others, and limited social relationships and adjustment within the school environment. The primary form of bullying identified was verbal bullying, particularly teasing related to family background, which perpetrators perceived as a joke but caused discomfort to the victims. Guidance and Counseling services play an important role in preventing and addressing bullying through preventive and curative approaches to help victims cope with the psychological impacts they experience.

title: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair in dynamic severe functional mitral regurgitation: A multicentre, randomised, controlled trial
abstractText: Abstract Background Functional mitral regurgitation (FMR) is a highly dynamic disease. Some patients exhibit only moderate (2+) FMR at rest, which deteriorates to moderate-to-severe or severe FMR (3+ or 4+) during stress, with effective regurgitant orifice area (EROA) increased ≥0.1 cm2—termed dynamic severe FMR. Observational studies link this condition to worse outcomes, with mitral valve intervention offering potential benefits; however, high-quality evidence remains deficient. Aims The Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair In dynaMic sEvere functional mitral Regurgitation (TIMER) trial aims to assess the safety and effectiveness of transcatheter edge-to-edge repair plus guideline-directed medical therapy versus guideline-directed medical therapy alone in symptomatic chronic heart failure patients with dynamic severe FMR, defined as moderate (2+) regurgitation at rest (EROA ≥0.2 cm2 to <0.3 cm2 and/or regurgitant volume (RVol) ≥30 mL/beat to <45 mL/beat), deteriorating to moderate-to-severe or severe (3+ or 4+) during handgrip stress echocardiography (stress EROA ≥0.30 cm2 and/or RVol ≥45 mL/beat), with EROA increased ≥0.1 cm2. Methods This prospective, multicentre, randomised trial enrols patients with dynamic severe FMR confirmed by a core laboratory using handgrip stress echocardiography, across 20 participating centres in China. Patients are randomised 1:1 to transcatheter edge-to-edge repair plus medical therapy or medical therapy alone. The primary endpoint is the composite incidence of cardiovascular death and all heart failure hospitalisations during the entire follow-up period. Conclusion This trial will provide critical evidence on transcatheter edge-to-edge repair in patients with dynamic severe FMR, informing future treatment recommendations. Trial registration number: NCT07197021

title: A Paired Lake–Land Observation Dataset of Mesoscale Lakes over the Tibetan Plateau for Analyzing Lake-induced Thermal and Moisture Modulation
abstractText: Abstract Lakes on the Tibetan Plateau are sensitive indicators of climate change and important regulators of local land–atmosphere exchanges. However, continuous in situ observations remain limited, especially for mesoscale lakes with lake areas of 100–500 km 2 . Moreover, paired lake–land observations are scarce, constraining accurate assessments of meteorological and surface-exchange differences between lake surfaces and their surrounding terrestrial environments. To address this lack of systematic and continuous observations, we present a paired lake–land observational dataset covering three representative lakes across the monsoon, monsoon–westerly transition, and westerly climate regions. The dataset provides continuous and consistently processed observations from lake and nearby land stations during 2019–23. The dataset includes automatic weather station observations, eddy correlation, radiation components, and corresponding nearby land-station observations. The main variables include air temperature, humidity, pressure, wind, precipitation, shortwave and longwave radiation, and sensible and latent heat fluxes. All records were processed using unified procedures, including time-continuity checks, missing-value flagging, unit conversion, format standardization, and quality control. Initial analyses reveal clear lake–land contrasts. Compared with nearby land stations, lake stations generally show smaller diurnal temperature ranges, higher warm-season humidity, stronger and more persistent winds, lower sensible heat flux, and higher latent heat flux. These results indicate that mesoscale lakes can substantially modify local thermal, moisture, and surface energy-exchange conditions. This dataset provides valuable support for studies of lake–land–atmosphere interactions, remote-sensing and reanalysis evaluation, and lake model improvement over the Tibetan Plateau. The dataset is available at the Tibetan Plateau Data Center and Science Data Bank.

Nutritional Composition and Socio-Economic Importance of the Shea Butter Caterpillar, Cirina forda (Westwood), as a Non-Wood Forest Product in Southern Taraba State, Nigeria
abstractText: Edible insects provide alternative nutrient sources and contribute to food security and rural livelihoods. This study assessed the nutritional composition and socioeconomic importance of the shea butter caterpillar, Cirina forda (Westwood), a seasonal non-wood forest product harvested from Vitellaria paradoxa trees in southern Taraba State, Nigeria. Fresh larvae were collected from selected trees across five local government areas, cleaned, and oven-dried at 60°C for 24 hours. Proximate composition was determined using AOAC (2012) methods, while minerals, vitamins, and antinutrients were analyzed spectrophotometrically. Statistical analyses employed t-tests and Duncan’s multiple range test at p ≤ .05. Socioeconomic data were collected through 200 questionnaires administered to collectors and traders. Drying significantly increased crude protein from 20.10% to 24.62% and reduced moisture from 10.74% to 6.44% (p < .05). Iron and zinc concentrations increased from 2.70 to 4.70 ppm and from 1.11 to 1.70 ppm, respectively, whereas sodium decreased from 3.63 to 3.16 ppm. Reported thiamine (vitamin B1) values declined from 97.8% to 10.9%, while retinol (vitamin A) was largely retained. Phytate and oxalate increased after drying. Among respondents, 56% were female, 39.5% were aged 18–25 years, and 48.5% belonged to households comprising 4–6 people. The socioeconomic findings indicated that C. forda contributed substantially to household livelihoods. Overall, the study identifies C. forda as a potential source of protein and minerals and an important rural livelihood resource. The processing-related changes in nutrients and antinutrients highlight the need for improved processing practices, alongside marketing interventions to support its socioeconomic value.

title: Pengaruh Attitude Towards Money, Financial Self Efficacy, dan Financial Risk Tolerance Terhadap Personal Financial Management Behavior Pada Generasi Z di Samarinda
abstractText: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh attitude towards money, financial self-efficacy, dan financial risk tolerance terhadap personal financial management behavior pada Generasi Z di Kota Samarinda. Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh kemudahan layanan keuangan digital, seperti mobile banking, e-wallet, dan PayLater, yang belum sepenuhnya diimbangi dengan kemampuan mengelola keuangan secara bijak. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif berlandaskan Theory of Planned Behavior dengan data primer yang dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner. Sampel berjumlah 180 responden yang ditentukan dengan teknik purposive sampling, yaitu Generasi Z berusia 17–29 tahun yang berdomisili di Samarinda. Data dianalisis menggunakan Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Square (SEM-PLS) dengan bantuan SmartPLS. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa attitude towards money berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap personal financial management behavior. Financial self-efficacy juga berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap personal financial management behavior. Sebaliknya, financial risk tolerance berpengaruh negatif dan tidak signifikan terhadap personal financial management behavior. Ketiga variabel secara bersama-sama mampu menjelaskan lebih dari separuh variasi personal financial management behavior, sedangkan sisanya dijelaskan oleh variabel lain di luar model. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa sikap positif terhadap uang dan keyakinan atas kemampuan diri merupakan faktor penting dalam membentuk perilaku pengelolaan keuangan Generasi Z, sedangkan toleransi terhadap risiko tidak menjadi penentu perilaku pengelolaan keuangan sehari-hari.

title: Assessment of Food Safety Knowledge, Hygiene Practices, and Microbial Contamination Risks Among Street Food Vendors in Urban Areas of Pakistan
abstractText: Street-vended foods provide affordable meals in Pakistan; however, inadequate hygiene, poor sanitation, and microbial contamination present significant public health challenges. To evaluate knowledge about food safety, hygienic practices, prevalence of microbial contamination and antimicrobial resistance amongst urban street food vendors. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted on 300 street food vendors from 5 major cities in Pakistan. Knowledge about food safety and hygienic practices was measured through structured questionnaires. Microbiological tests were performed on 300 food samples, 150 environmental swabs and antimicrobial susceptibility performed on 120 bacterial isolates. Results: The average score achieved by participants for food safety knowledge was 14.2 ± 5.1. There was a high percentage of individuals with poor knowledge (42.0%). 51.0% of vendors did not follow adequate hygienic practices. Only 36.0% washed their hands appropriately and 65.7% did not have adequate refrigeration. Microbial contamination was present in 61.7% of food samples. This included Staphylococcus aureus (32.0%), Escherichia coli (26.0%), Bacillus cereus (23.0%) and Salmonella spp. (11.0%). Meat products (76.7%) and fresh salads (75.0%) exhibited the highest contamination frequencies. Pollution of the environment was observed in 59.3% of swabs and multidrug resistance was found in 35.0% of bacterial isolates. These findings emphasize the need for better food safety education, sanitation infrastructure, hygiene monitoring and microbiological surveillance to reduce the risks of foodborne illness.

The influence of sample size, modelling algorithms, and hyperparameters on bootstrap-based prediction stability in clinical prediction model development: An empirical study using the HOPE dataset
abstractText: Abstract Background The stability of clinical prediction models has emerged as an important factor in model development. Models producing unstable or unreliable predictions can ultimately lead to improper clinical decisions and harm patients when applied in clinical practice. Previous studies have highlighted the role of sample size in prediction stability, with larger samples delivering increased stability. However, the role of other modelling decisions remains unclear. This study considered three modifiable factors influencing the stability of predictions: sample size, modelling algorithm (i.e., parametric regression and machine learning algorithms), and hyperparameter tuning. Methods We used the previously published HOPE dataset to develop a prediction model for anxiety at palliative care admission, incorporating 34 candidate predictors. To examine the impact of sample size, we generated seven datasets of varying sizes through random sampling. A total of 21 modelling scenarios were evaluated by combining these datasets with three modelling approaches: LASSO logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost. Models were tuned using cross-validation and assessed for discrimination (AUC) and calibration. Prediction stability was evaluated using a bootstrap-based framework, including the mean absolute prediction error (MAPE) and related instability plots. Results In this clinical dataset, larger sample sizes were associated with lower average MAPE and a higher proportion of predictions with MAPE ≤ 5% for LASSO, with limited additional changes beyond the reference size ( n = 3,875). LASSO also showed lower AUC optimism and calibration slopes closer to 1 across increasing sample sizes. Random forest and XGBoost showed higher discrimination than LASSO in some scenarios, but had higher average MAPE, a lower proportion of predictions with MAPE ≤5%, and calibration slopes further from 1 across sample sizes. Conservative hyperparameter settings, such as shallower trees and slower learning rates, were associated with lower MAPE but slightly lower discrimination. Conclusions Our results provide empirical insights into bootstrap-based prediction stability in clinical prediction model development. Model stability appeared to depend not only on sample size but also on modelling approach and hyperparameter tuning. For machine learning models, considering stability alongside marginal gains in accuracy may be important. Further research should explore alternative validation strategies and optimal tuning practices to guide robust clinical prediction model development.

title: Pengembangan Keterampilan Digital melalui Edukasi Teknologi IoT Berbasis ESP32 bagi Siswa SMK AKP Beringin Lubuk Pakam
abstractText: The development of Internet of Things (IoT) technology requires Vocational High School (SMK) students to possess technical skills relevant to workforce needs, particularly in microcontroller programming and electronic device control. However, most students at SMK AKP Beringin Lubuk Pakam, especially from the Motorcycle Engineering (TSM) and Computer and Network Engineering (TKJ) programs, remained limited to basic theoretical understanding of microcontrollers and lacked hands-on experience in real IoT projects. This community service activity aimed to develop students' digital skills through education on ESP32-based IoT technology. The activity was carried out as a one-day workshop using a Project-Based Learning (PjBL) approach, involving 20 students (7 from TSM and 13 from TKJ) at SMK AKP Lubuk Pakam on 4 August 2026. The stages included delivery of basic IoT and ESP32 concepts, hands-on assembly and programming practice using the Arduino IDE, and an interactive discussion session. Improvement in participants' understanding was measured through a pretest and posttest. The evaluation results showed an increase in the average score from 52.0 (pretest) to 82.5 (posttest), a relative improvement of 58.7%. All participants successfully installed the Arduino IDE, wrote basic programs, and assembled and tested simple sensors and actuators. These findings indicate that a hands-on, project-based learning approach effectively improves the technical IoT skills of vocational students within a relatively short period, while also opening opportunities for program continuity through school-based robotics/electronics extracurricular activities.

title: Clinical expertise and cognitive reflection predict fewer misconceptions in Bayesian diagnostic reasoning
abstractText: Abstract Background For many years, research has consistently confirmed that even medical experts fail to solve Bayesian diagnostic tasks. These tasks require correctly estimating a diagnostic test’s positive predictive value based on sensitivity, specificity, and the disease’s prevalence. Previous research has primarily focused on improving task presentation, for example by using natural frequencies or visual aids. The present study introduces the Medical Bayesian Performance Score (MBPS), a confidence-weighted measure that distinguishes confidently held misconceptions from missing concepts. Participants completed eight medical Bayesian diagnostic tasks and rated their confidence after each response. Using this approach, we examined whether medical knowledge, clinical expertise, and cognitive reflection are associated with performance in Bayesian diagnostic reasoning. Methods In an online survey, we compared MBPS values via t tests along two independent variables: (a) medical knowledge (physician group: N p = 30 vs. student control group: N s = 56) and (b) clinical expertise within the physician group (specialists and senior physicians: N e = 19 vs. resident physicians: N r = 11). Furthermore, we analyzed correlations between MBPS values and Cognitive Reflection Test (CRT) scores. Results Physicians did not achieve significantly higher MBPS values than the student control group. In contrast, specialists and senior physicians scored significantly higher than resident physicians. Across all groups, average MBPS values were negative, indicating that confidence-weighted incorrect responses outweighed confidence-weighted correct responses, a pattern consistent with misconceptions. Furthermore, higher CRT scores correlated significantly with higher MBPS values. Conclusions The MBPS provides a complementary perspective to conventional accuracy measures by distinguishing misconceptions from missing concepts and linking Bayesian diagnostic reasoning research with conceptual change theory. Consistent with this perspective, our findings suggest that formal medical knowledge alone was not associated with fewer misconceptions, whereas greater clinical expertise and higher cognitive reflection were. Future research should evaluate evidence-based conceptual change interventions for medical education, such as specific refutation-based training, as a means of improving Bayesian diagnostic reasoning.

title: IMPROVING EFL STUDENTS' WRITING SKILLS THROUGH DIGITAL LEARNING PLATFORMS
abstractText: Writing is a complex skill for EFL (English as a Foreign Language) learners because it involves grammatical competence, vocabulary knowledge, idea organization, and the ability to convey meaning coherently. Technological developments have introduced various digital platforms that can support writing instruction, particularly through collaborative features, feedback, and assessment tools. This article aims to examine the roles and uses of digital learning platforms in EFL writing instruction based on previous research. This study employed a literature review method involving 15 scholarly publications published between 2021 and 2025. The data were analyzed thematically by categorizing the findings according to the functions of technology in writing instruction. The review identified three major themes. First, Google Docs supports collaborative writing through shared text production and editing, interaction among learners, and engagement in the writing process. Second, artificial intelligence-based technologies, particularly ChatGPT, provide alternative sources of feedback and support for writing revision, although the accuracy and relevance of their outputs still require evaluation and teacher guidance. Third, AI-based tools can serve as additional resources for writing assessment; however, differences between human and AI scoring indicate that automated assessment cannot fully replace human judgment. This review concludes that digital platforms serve complementary functions in EFL writing instruction, but their use should be aligned with learning objectives, learner characteristics, and appropriate pedagogical strategies. The limitations of this review include its publication coverage and the predominance of studies focusing on Google Docs and AI-based tools. Future research should explore other digital platforms and investigate the influence of digital literacy, teacher guidance, and technology access on EFL writing instruction. ABSTRAK Menulis merupakan salah satu keterampilan yang kompleks bagi pembelajar EFL (English as a Foreign Language) karena melibatkan penguasaan tata bahasa, kosakata, pengorganisasian gagasan, dan penyampaian makna secara koheren. Perkembangan teknologi menghadirkan berbagai platform digital yang dapat dimanfaatkan untuk mendukung proses pembelajaran menulis, terutama melalui fitur kolaborasi, umpan balik, dan penilaian. Artikel ini bertujuan untuk mengkaji peran dan pemanfaatan platform pembelajaran digital dalam pembelajaran keterampilan menulis EFL berdasarkan hasil penelitian terdahulu. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode kajian literatur terhadap 15 publikasi ilmiah yang terbit pada periode 2021–2025. Data dianalisis secara tematik dengan mengelompokkan temuan berdasarkan fungsi teknologi dalam pembelajaran menulis. Hasil kajian mengidentifikasi tiga tema utama. Pertama, Google Docs mendukung penulisan kolaboratif melalui penyusunan dan penyuntingan teks bersama, interaksi antarpembelajar, serta keterlibatan dalam proses menulis. Kedua, teknologi berbasis kecerdasan buatan, khususnya ChatGPT, menyediakan alternatif umpan balik dan dukungan revisi tulisan, meskipun ketepatan dan relevansi hasilnya tetap memerlukan evaluasi serta pendampingan guru. Ketiga, perangkat berbasis AI dapat dimanfaatkan sebagai sumber tambahan dalam penilaian tulisan, tetapi perbedaan hasil penilaian antara manusia dan AI menunjukkan bahwa penilaian otomatis belum dapat sepenuhnya menggantikan pertimbangan penilai manusia. Kajian ini menyimpulkan bahwa platform digital memiliki fungsi yang saling melengkapi dalam pembelajaran menulis EFL, tetapi pemanfaatannya perlu disesuaikan dengan tujuan pembelajaran, karakteristik pembelajar, dan strategi pedagogis. Keterbatasan kajian terletak pada cakupan publikasi dan dominasi penelitian mengenai Google Docs serta perangkat berbasis AI. Penelitian selanjutnya perlu mengeksplorasi platform lain dan menguji pengaruh literasi digital, pendampingan guru, serta akses teknologi terhadap proses pembelajaran menulis EFL.

title: Effect of cardiac-index guided intraoperative haemodynamic therapy on postoperative outcome in non-cardiac surgery patients – a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstractText: Abstract Background Optimal perioperative haemodynamic management is essential to reduce postoperative complications. While multiple technologies allow for advanced monitoring, clear evidence on the effectiveness of Cardiac Index-guided goal-directed therapy (CI-GDT) compared to standard care in non-cardiac surgery is lacking. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to investigate the impact of CI-GDT on postoperative outcome. Methods A systematic search using PubMed and Web of Science (2010–2025) identified randomised controlled trials (RCT) comparing CI-GDT to standard care in adult non-cardiac surgery. Study selection and data extraction were conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and registered under PROSPERO (CRD420251058399). Odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) and 95% prediction intervals (PI) were calculated using a random-effects model. Risk of bias was assessed via the RoB 2 tool. Heterogeneity was quantified with I 2 , τ 2 , and Cochran’s Q. Reporting bias was evaluated by funnel plots, Egger’s test, and trim-and-fill method. Sensitivity was assessed by leave-one-out analysis. Results Twenty-one RCTs were included, of which 20 contributed data to the meta-analysis of postoperative complications. CI-GDT significantly reduced the incidence of postoperative complications (OR .59 [.45–.78]; PI .20–1.74; I 2 = 62.9%). Mortality did not differ significantly between groups (OR 0.77 [.57–1.05]; I 2 = 0%). Funnel plot and Egger’s test indicated no significant publication bias ( p =.15). Leave-one-out analysis confirmed robustness of findings. Trim-and-fill did not suggest missing studies. Certainty of evidence was graded high. Discussion/conclusion CI-GDT was associated with a lower incidence of patients experiencing at least one postoperative complication, whereas mortality did not differ significantly. However, substantial heterogeneity and a prediction interval crossing the null indicate that the benefit may not be consistent across clinical settings. These findings do not establish an independent advantage of CI targeting over other GDT strategies.

title: Acidic C─H Functionalization to Access Ketoalkyl-Substituted Quinazolinones by Visible-Light Photoredox Catalysis
abstractText: Abstract Herein, we report a novel visible-light-mediated radical cascade for the synthesis of ketoalkyl-substituted fused quinazolinones. This green and highly efficient method employs a readily available iridium photocatalyst and utilizes acetone as both the reaction medium and a C3-building block, enabled by a benzoyl peroxide (BPO)-mediated activation strategy for its α-acidic C─H bond. Contrary to the conventional wisdom that electrophilic oxygen-centered radicals preferentially abstract hydridic C─H bonds, our strategy operates via a distinct pathway that selectively targets acidic C─H bonds. This protocol is compatible with a wide variety of N-cyanamide alkenes as well as other ketones and activated methylene compounds (e.g., esters, acetonitrile, nitromethane). Mechanistic studies, including radical trapping experiments, kinetic isotope effect (KIE) measurements, and Stern–Volmer quenching studies are conducted to support proposed mechanism.

Procaine and Doxorubicin Coloaded Microspheres for Painless and Potent Transarterial Chemoembolization
abstractText: Abstract Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) is the standard treatment for intermediate-stage hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, its clinical efficacy is severely limited by postembolization syndrome (PES) and the physical vascular barrier induced by embolization. To address these limitations, we developed multifunctional polyvinyl alcohol embolization microspheres modified with polydopamine and coloaded with procaine (PCA) and doxorubicin (DOX), termed pDA-PVA/PCA-DOX. MD/MM-PBSA simulations and physicochemical characterization confirmed that the pDA coating enabled efficient coloading of both drugs via hydrogen bonding and π–π stacking, with the particle size meeting clinical requirements for TACE. The loading capacities of PCA and DOX in this codelivery system reached 4.6 and 4.8 times those of commercial microspheres, respectively. The adsorption kinetics fitted a pseudo-second-order model, and the microspheres exhibited distinct pH-responsive release behavior. In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated that the sustained release of PCA downregulated proinflammatory cytokines, upregulated IL-10 expression, and reduced macrophage infiltration, thereby exerting analgesic and anti-inflammatory effects. Furthermore, the codelivery of PCA and DOX exerted synergistic antitumor efficacy with a coefficient of drug interaction (CDI) of 0.62–0.63, significantly inhibiting the proliferation, migration, and invasion of HCC cells. In mouse subcutaneous xenograft and rabbit VX2 liver tumor TACE models, the pDA-PVA/PCA-DOX significantly suppressed tumor growth, downregulated angiogenesis-related markers including VEGF, EGFR, and CD31, and modulated the immune microenvironment by increasing intratumoral infiltration of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells. Additionally, the pDA-PVA/PCA-DOX exhibited favorable biocompatibility and hemocompatibility, causing no persistent hepatic or renal toxicity post-TACE. Collectively, this multifunctional coloaded microsphere system integrates efficient embolization, anti-inflammation, analgesia, synergistic chemotherapy, and microenvironment modulation, providing experimental evidence for optimizing TACE therapeutic strategies.

abstractText: تُعدّ الرطوبة من أكثر المشكلات شيوعًا التي تهدد متانة المباني وسلامة شاغليها. تتناول هذه الورقة، بمنهج وصفي تحليلي، أضرار الرطوبة في أربعة عناصر إنشائية هي القواعد والسملات، والجدران، والأعمدة، والأسقف، من حيث مصادرها وأنواعها وآثارها في الخرسانة وحديد التسليح، وطرق تشخيصها، وأساليب علاجها والوقاية منها بالعزل المائي والمعالجات الكيميائية وتحسين الصرف والتهوية. وتخلص الورقة إلى أن غياب العزل المائي أو سوء تنفيذه من أبرز أسباب التدهور الإنشائي، وأن الوقاية أثناء التصميم والتنفيذ أقل كلفة وأكثر فاعلية من العلاج بعد ظهور الضرر، وتقدّم توصيات عملية للمهندسين والمنفذين.

title: Pembelajaran Berbasis Bermain melalui Pengenalan Huruf Abjad, Menggambar, dan Mewarnai bagi Anak di Lembaga Pendidikan Inklusi PGTK Kusuma Bangsa Kota Bima
abstractText: Kegiatan pengabdian ini dilaksanakan oleh mahasiswa Kuliah Kerja Nyata (KKN) Kelompok 4 Kelurahan Paruga STIE Bima di Lembaga Pendidikan Inklusi PGTK Kusuma Bangsa, Kota Bima, di bawah arahan dosen pembimbing lapangan. Lembaga ini melayani kelompok reguler usia 2–6 tahun dan kelompok tunalaras/tunagrahita usia 2–9 tahun, sehingga pembelajarannya menuntut fleksibilitas yang lebih tinggi dibandingkan satuan PAUD pada umumnya. Program berlangsung dalam 13 pertemuan pada Selasa 4–26 Agustus 2026 dengan empat kegiatan: pengenalan huruf abjad, menggambar, mewarnai, dan bermain. Setiap pertemuan melibatkan enam mahasiswa secara bergilir sebagai pendamping kelompok kecil. Pelaksanaan meliputi observasi awal, perencanaan bersama guru, pelaksanaan pembelajaran, dan refleksi pascakegiatan. Hasil pengamatan menunjukkan bahwa anak dari kelompok reguler maupun kelompok berkebutuhan khusus dapat dilibatkan dalam keempat kegiatan ketika dilayani dalam kelompok kecil, dengan koreksi dan penguatan diberikan langsung oleh pendamping, sedangkan perubahan perkembangan yang menetap belum dapat disimpulkan dari program berdurasi singkat ini. Kegiatan ini memperlihatkan bahwa rasio pendamping yang lebih rapat menjadi prasyarat praktis bagi pembelajaran terdiferensiasi di kelas inklusif dengan keragaman kebutuhan yang tinggi.
